text: NIO absorbed a RMB 10,000/vehicle purchase-tax subsidy on ES8 orders locked through 30 April 2026 and then discontinued it mid-Q2 — Deutsche Bank named that discontinuation as a cause of the June ES8 order shortfall. ES8 (Gen 3) was 33,474 units of Q2's 107,658, so removing RMB 10,000/unit from even ~18,000 Q2 deliveries retains ~RMB 180m of margin, which is the whole of Deutsche Bank's ~RMB 180m Q2 non-GAAP net income estimate. The 2.1% unit miss versus the 110-115k guide was in part the price paid for that margin, not purely demand weakness.
why_not_priced: The delivery miss is a published monthly number every terminal has; the subsidy withdrawal that partly caused it is a line item disclosed only in Chinese-language promo terms and a CnEVPost analyst note, and it works in the opposite direction on the P&L. If the market had joined the two, the stock would not be sitting at its 52-week low on a 'profitability doubt' narrative into a quarter where the per-unit subsidy drag was actively being removed — you would see previews framing the unit miss as margin-accretive, and there are none.

text: NIO's 20-F for FY2025, filed 2026-04-10, discloses that headcount fell to 35,032 from 45,635 — 10,603 jobs, the sharpest single-year cut in its history — with product and software development down 40% to 6,912 from 11,528 and 'user experience' (sales, marketing, service) down 30.8% to 16,885 from 24,410. NIO never gave aggregate numbers during 2025, calling it 'organizational optimization'. Q2 2026 volume was +29% sequentially (107,658 vs 83,465) against that reduced cost base.
why_not_priced: The aggregate figures exist only in an employee table deep in a 20-F; the wire coverage of that filing (StockTitan, Yahoo) carried the headline 'NIO files its annual report' with no headcount content, and the only outlets that extracted the numbers were a niche EV site and a LinkedIn post. If this were priced you would see it in the preview arithmetic as an explicit opex step-down, and consensus would not still be modelling a full-year loss of CN¥1.69/share. The negative tail is real too: cutting sales and service headcount 31% while launching two brands is a demand-execution risk, which is why the band spans zero.

text: NIO's year-on-year growth rate collapses mechanically from the August number onward on base effects, and 1 September is NIO's established monthly-delivery publication slot, so the August figure plausibly lands in the same tape as Q2 results and the Q3 guide. July 2026 was 35,934, +71.0% YoY against a July 2025 base of ~21,017. But August 2025 was 31,305 and September 2025 was 34,749 (Q3 2025 total 87,071) — the base steps up ~49% in one month. Bottom-up August 2026 indicators point to roughly flat-to-modestly-up sequentially (third-gen ES8's latest 10,000 units took 30 days as of 21 August; Onvo L60 at 3,201 units in the first 28 days), implying Q3 near 113-118k and YoY growth roughly halving to ~+30%.
why_not_priced: The sell-side has these comps; the marginal holder of a $4.37 ADS does not, and the narrative in circulation is the '+71% year-on-year' July headline. The structural half of this is the sharper point: NIO filed monthly delivery 6-Ks on 2026-06-01, 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-03 for the prior month, so 1 September is the slot for August, and no aggregator flags that this print carries three releases at once. If the market had this, the front-expiry implied move would sit above the 9.76% single-event level to reflect a compound catalyst, and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 0.32.

text: NIO's smart-driving chief Ren Shaoqing has founded a separately registered embodied-AI/physical-AI-foundation-model company that has already reached a unicorn-level valuation, and NIO reportedly plans to make a strategic investment in it while Ren stays on as NIO's smart-driving chief. Reported 21 and 24 August 2026, after NIO's last public communication.
why_not_priced: It broke in Chinese-language and China-EV trade press in the nine days before the print and has no US wire pickup; NIO has not confirmed it and it is not in any filing. It is a divided-attention and related-party-transaction question in the single most valuation-sensitive function, and it is the kind of item that gets asked on the 8:00 a.m. call rather than in the release. If it were priced there would be a sell-side note on smart-driving key-man risk; there is none. Sign is genuinely ambiguous — on a $4 stock with calls bid, a robotics affiliation can be read as a positive optionality headline, which is why the band crosses zero.

text: NIO has now missed its own delivery guidance in consecutive disclosures — June 2026 came in at 40,597 against a 42,900-47,900 guide, and Q2 at 107,658 against 110,000-115,000 — so whatever Q3 unit and revenue range management gives on 1 September starts with an impaired discount factor.
why_not_priced: Weakest of the five and closest to priced — the individual misses are public. What is not in the coverage is that they are consecutive and both attributable to NIO's own promotional withdrawals rather than to the market, which changes how a fresh guide should be read. Sized small precisely because most of this is in the -9.2% twenty-day drift already.

Heidmar's earnings releases are the mechanical trigger for refreshing the resale prospectus covering 11,080,332 shares for B. Riley Principal Capital II: the 424B3 filed 2026-03-24 exists solely to supplement the 20 June 2025 prospectus 'with the information contained in our report on Form 6-K, filed with the SEC on March 24, 2026' - the same day as the Q4 print. The same pattern holds for 2025-08-12 (two 424B3s the day after the 2025-08-11 print), 2025-09-29 (424B3 and 6-K same day) and 2025-11-06, and a POS AM followed the Q1 print by two days. That resale registration was re-declared effective 2026-06-10, so 2026-09-01 is the first print under the refreshed shelf, and 11,080,332 shares is 170% of the company's entire non-affiliate share count.
why_not_priced: The baseline records 5 of 6 prints closing down with a 5.13% median reaction but explicitly sets history_usable to 0 and discounts the pattern as possibly describing a dead reporting regime. Nobody has supplied the mechanism, and the mechanism is what makes the pattern forward-looking rather than sample noise. If the market had focused on it there would be visible pre-print weakness in the last five sessions beyond the observed -1.42%, a discount to the sector's Q2 re-rating rather than a 24% 20-day run-up, and the covering analysts would be flagging equity-line dilution rather than modelling flat revenue. No 424B3 or draw disclosure exists yet for Q2, so the size of the refresh is unknown to holders.

text: The two-analyst FY2026 revenue forecast of $74.29m implies roughly $18.6m per quarter for Q2-Q4 against Q1 2026 actual of $18.4m - i.e. essentially flat, and below Q4 2025's $25.1m - while the spot rates that drive both of Heidmar's revenue lines rose 47-82% sequentially in Q2 (Frontline realised VLCC $103,500 to $152,700/day, Suezmax $72,400 to $111,500/day, LR2/Aframax $50,700 to $92,400/day, Q1 to Q2 2026), and the five vessels added in March/April 2026 contribute a full quarter for the first time. Heidmar's Q1 revenue was $5.68m trade revenues plus $12.67m voyage and time charter revenues from eight vessels employed on short-term spot/TC voyages versus one a year earlier; the Q2 2025 comparative is $9.6m total revenue and $0.5m adjusted net income.
why_not_priced: The rate data is public but the translation into this company's gross-freight-linked P&L is not: this name has one to two covering analysts who got Q1 exactly backwards (revenue below estimate, EPS beat by roughly 1,000%), demonstrating they do not model the structure. If the gap were priced the FY2026 revenue line would have been revised above Q4 2025's run-rate after the peer prints of the last three weeks, and HMR's 20-day move would look like a tanker-equity re-rating rather than -15% from its own 52-week high. snippet_only on the Frontline TCE figures (globenewswire returned 503 to direct fetch; figures taken from search snippet of that release).

text: Heidmar's fee-earning commercially managed fleet was effectively flat through Q2 2026: the 2025 Form 20-F filed 2026-04-30 states 'The Capital vessels compose 25 of the 49 vessels currently managed by Heidmar', while the 2026-07-07 release states the company manages 'around 50 vessels under commercial management and 16 vessels under technical management' - and that is after an acquisition (Q-Shipping B.V., effective 2026-07-01) that the company itself says added nine vessels to the managed fleet. Heidmar has issued no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19, the longest such gap since the de-SPAC, against five additions announced for Q1.
why_not_priced: This requires putting two documents filed ten weeks apart side by side; neither figure is a headline and no aggregator carries a vessel-count time series for this name. If it were priced the equity would not have run 24% in 20 days on a platform-growth narrative, and the sell-side FY revenue number would show a decelerating vessel-count assumption rather than a flat one. The count as at 30 June is not public and will be disclosed for the first time tomorrow.

text: Heidmar has had no Chief Financial Officer since 31 May 2026 - Niki Fotiou ceased in the role and CEO Pankaj Khanna took over 'the finance function' pending a search - and no successor has been announced as of 2026-08-31, three months later. Q2 2026 is therefore the first quarter this company has closed, audited-reviewed and reported without a CFO. Separately, Heidmar has furnished no Form 6-K since 2026-05-28 despite three subsequent material announcements (CFO departure, Nasdaq compliance regained, Q-Shipping acquisition).
why_not_priced: The June departure was press-released and is stale news; what is not priced is the three-month absence of a replacement and the fact that this print is the first one produced without a CFO, which raises the odds of thin disclosure, no quantitative outlook, and a call at which the CEO answers financial questions alone. If holders had focused on it the stock would not have re-rated 24% into the print, and the coverage would carry a governance discount rather than a growth multiple. The vacancy is verifiable only by absence - there is no announcement to aggregate.

text: Only 6,498,572 of Heidmar's 58,991,997 outstanding shares are held by non-affiliates - an 11.0% float worth about $9.0m at spot - against 20-day average volume of 50,189 shares and short interest of just 127,609 shares. The prospectus states verbatim: 'As of May 20, 2026, we had 58,991,997 Common Shares outstanding, of which 6,498,572 shares were held by non-affiliates of our company.'
why_not_priced: The number sits on an inside page of a post-effective amendment, not on any quote page; every screener reports the 58.99m share count and a float five to nine times the true one. It is not directionally priced because it cannot be - it is a convexity fact, and the baseline has no option chain at all with which to express it, so nothing in the price states a reaction width. Negligible short interest (1.9% of float) also means there is no crowded position to unwind, so a genuine beat has no natural seller.

text: Three Heidmar directors filed Form 144s to sell 244,862 shares between 2026-06-11 and 2026-07-06 - Andreas Konialidis 113,287 shares ($165,400), Vasileios Loutradis 126,575 shares ($138,699) and Andre Lockhorst 5,000 shares ($5,950) - equal to about 3.8% of the entire non-affiliate float and roughly five sessions of average volume. As a foreign private issuer there is no Form 4 to confirm execution.
why_not_priced: Form 144 is an intent-to-sell notice that no insider-trade aggregator reliably surfaces for FPIs because there is no matching Form 4, so the standard insider-transaction feeds show nothing after 2026-04-03. If this had registered with holders, the 24% 20-day run-up would have met visible insider supply in the tape and the coverage would mention it. The relevant scale is against a 6.5m-share float, not the 59m share count everyone screens on.

text: Half of Heidmar's fee base sits with one related party that has just been separately capitalised: the 20-F states the Capital vessels are 25 of 49 managed vessels and 'accounted for 37% of our total revenues from the Pools during the year ended December 31, 2025', and Capital Tankers Corp. listed on Euronext Growth Oslo on 2026-03-17 after raising about USD 500m, with a fleet of 30 super-eco crude tankers of which 21 are newbuildings delivering 2026-2028 plus options on 13 more.
why_not_priced: A Euronext Growth Oslo listing is outside the coverage set of anyone following a $81m Nasdaq microcap, and no US aggregator links the two names. The read is two-sided and unpriced in either direction: 21 newbuilds from a counterparty that already supplies 25 of 49 managed vessels is the largest identifiable growth pipeline in Heidmar's model, and equally the largest single point of failure if a now independently funded Capital Tankers internalises commercial management. Neither possibility appears in any Heidmar-facing note. snippet_only on the fleet composition.

The syndicated Q1 FY27 consensus revenue of $9.47bn (+10.4% on the $8,578m year-ago base) sits roughly a point below what Medtronic's own 3 June quarterly guidance implies — 11.5% to 12.0% organic growth plus a 'neutral to $50 million' FX tailwind plus acquired revenue from CathWorks/Scientia/SPR, i.e. about $9.55-9.65bn — while consensus EPS of $1.39 is exactly the midpoint of the guided $1.38-$1.40; the same one-point gap exists at the full-year level ($38.85bn consensus vs 6.75-7.25% organic on $36,364m plus 0-1% FX plus M&A). The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management [sizing note removed]. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.
why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the reconciliation of a consensus print against the company's own quarterly guide, and the inconsistency is visible only as an internal contradiction in the estimate set (EPS on guidance, revenue below it). If it were priced, previews would be flagging a 'low bar on revenue' rather than quoting the $9.47bn as the bar; instead Zacks' preview quotes it straight. I keep the size small and let the band cross zero because the marginal holder of a mega-cap trades the buy-side bar, not the Zacks bar, and MDT has twice in the last four prints sold off on a headline beat.

text: As of 2026-08-31 no registration statement or tender-offer document for the MiniMed split-off exists on EDGAR: Medtronic (CIK 1613103) has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-03 and no S-4/Schedule TO, and MiniMed Group (CIK 2062583) shows no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO on or after 2026-06-01. On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. An exchange offer needs a registered offer document and a ~20-business-day offer period, so with nothing on file at end-August the 'upside from early separation' has not begun to be executed. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.
why_not_priced: This is an absence, and absences do not generate wire copy — there is no article saying 'Medtronic has not yet filed the exchange-offer S-4'. If the market had priced a slip, previews would be discussing whether FY27 guidance gets re-based rather than repeating the June 'full twelve months of Diabetes' framing. The band crosses zero because the standard sequencing is to launch an exchange offer immediately after a quarterly release, so the same fact can flip to a positive on 1 September.

text: The Investor Day Medtronic committed to on 2025-08-19, when it added two Elliott-adjacent directors and formed the Growth and Operating Committees, was promised for 'mid-calendar year 2026' and was to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the committees' margin and efficiency targets. Mid-2026 has passed and, as of 2026-08-31, no date has been announced: the June Q4 call did not mention it and the Medtronic newsroom shows only three releases since (21 July Touch Surgery Aide, 6 August Affera CE Mark, 20 August dividend).
why_not_priced: A missed soft deadline on an event with no announced date produces no headline and no estimate revision, so there is nothing for the tape to have reflected. If it were priced you would see notes handicapping the margin target, as happened around every peer's activist-driven capital markets day. The 1 September call is the natural venue to set a date, so the sign is genuinely two-sided and the band is wide.

text: Boston Scientific reported on 2026-07-29 that its electrophysiology business grew only 3% in the US in calendar Q2 2026 (versus 23% internationally), citing competitive pressure and noting that US PFA is now roughly 80% of the AFib market. Calendar Q2 covers about two-thirds of Medtronic's fiscal Q1 (25 April to 31 July), and Cardiac Ablation Solutions — up 78% globally and 124% in the US in Medtronic's Q4 FY26 — is the single largest contributor to the 6.75-7.25% FY27 organic guide. The datapoint reads as continued Affera/Sphere-9 share gain in the quarter Medtronic is about to report, but the same disclosure caps how much market growth is left.
why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I am sizing it accordingly. MDT rose 3.2% on 27-28 July, i.e. before the BSX print, and only 0.8% on 29 July itself, so the tape does not look like it repriced Medtronic's CAS line on the read-across. But the 80%-penetration remark is the bearish half of the same disclosure and cuts the other way, which is exactly why a single number here is not worth more than a few tenths.

MMED's short interest is 5,896,696 shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement against a public float of 27.96m shares (Medtronic holds ~90% of 280.84m shares outstanding) - i.e. ~21% of float with 5.1-5.7 days to cover - yet the most widely syndicated short-interest pages display it as '2.1% of float' because they divide by shares outstanding rather than float; the position was built from 1,341,393 shares at the 2026-03-13 settlement to a 6,570,728 peak on 2026-06-30 and has been reduced only ~10% since, while the stock has roughly doubled off its 2026-05-15 low of $10.65.
why_not_priced: There is no functioning listed market in which to express this: total option open interest is 833 contracts and the ATM bid-ask is 174% of mid, so the +22 vol-point 25-delta skew is a scarcity/hedging artifact in a 28m-share float rather than a statement of informed bearishness - if a real bearish consensus were priced you would also see it in the sell-side, which is 13 analysts at Strong Buy with BofA raising its target to $24 in mid-August. And the screen figure marginal holders actually read says 2.1%, not 21%, so the crowding is invisible at the point of decision.

text: The IPO lock-up lapses on the morning of the print: the 424B4 is dated 2026-03-05 and EDGAR full-text search confirms it contains the phrase '180 days after the date of this prospectus' (180 days from 2026-03-05 is 2026-09-01), and that lock-up binds Medtronic's ~252.9m shares as well as every officer and director; as of 2026-08-31 Medtronic's EDGAR submissions show no S-4, no Schedule TO and no 425 has ever been filed, so the split-off exchange offer is not launched and becomes launchable from this print forward against a stated intent to finish the separation in calendar 2026.
why_not_priced: The coincidence of dates is arithmetic nobody publishes: MMED reports at 3:45 a.m. PDT on the exact day the restricted period ends, and the same morning Medtronic reports and could file the S-4/TO under Rule 162 early commencement. In a split-off exchange offer the arbitrage is long parent / short subsidiary, so announcement day is mechanically negative for MMED. If this were priced you would see it in the borrow and in front-expiry put open interest, and instead total OI across the whole 2026-09-18 chain is 833 contracts. You would also see the stock discounted, and instead it sits 3.5% off its 52-week high. Coverage frames the separation as a positive de-overhang event and does not date the launch window.

text: Q1 FY27 is a 14-week quarter and the two halves of the arithmetic sit in two different companies' disclosures: MiniMed's CFO said on 2026-06-03 that 'excluding the extra week, we expect Q1 growth to be roughly similar to Q4' (Q4 FY26 organic was 8.7%), while Medtronic's CFO quantified the extra selling week as '500 to 600 basis points to first-quarter growth' - stacking them implies MMED prints roughly 14% organic growth, versus the '~10% organic FY27 outlook' that quote pages and screens carry as the company's guidance.

Nasdaq shows a single estimate for MMED and stockanalysis.com carries no quarterly estimate at all, only the FY2027 annual $3.42bn. That is the signature of a name where the headline growth number is not modelled at the quarter level, so a ~14% organic print reads as a large acceleration against a '10%' anchor to exactly the momentum and retail flow that a 28m float is most sensitive to. If this were priced there would be a published quarterly consensus above the FY run-rate and a preview note explaining the 53rd week.

MiniMed's fiscal Q1 FY27 is a 98-day (14-week) quarter — 2026-04-25 through 2026-07-31 — against a 91-day (13-week) prior-year quarter (2025-04-26 through 2025-07-25); the entire 53rd week of FY27 falls in this single quarter, and MiniMed's own definition of 'Organic Revenue Growth' adjusts only for FX and Italian payback accruals, NOT for extra weeks, so the organic-growth headline will print roughly double the 8.7% it printed for Q4 FY26 on calendar alone. The dates are established by the company's own filings: FY26 ended 2026-04-24 (Q4 exhibit 99.1), the year-ago quarter ended 2025-07-25 (Medtronic 10-Q mdt-20250725), and this quarter ends 2026-07-31 (the 2026-07-20 announcement).

If the marginal holder had internalised that Q1 organic growth is mechanically ~15% rather than ~9%, you would expect a visible pre-print run-up rather than 20d +4.55% / 5d +0.15% at exactly the $20 IPO price, and you would not see two of five analysts (BofA $27->$20 on 18 May, Wells $26->$22 on 4 June) cutting targets into it. The first session is priced off the release headline, and the only prior print — a GAAP loss of $(0.68) that still produced +15.93% — is direct evidence this name trades off the growth line, not the EPS line.

text: About $20m of Q4 FY26's $837m reported revenue was not product demand: the 'Other' line jumped to $22m from $2m a year earlier and the footnote defines it as 'net sales generated from the sales of smart insulin pens and services. Amounts in this line also reflect adjustments to the Company's Italian payback accruals' — a legal-accrual release that is expressly excluded from the organic growth definition. Anyone extrapolating the $837m base into Q1 has carried a one-off forward, and the underlying Italian exposure is live rather than settled: the Council of State (Ordinance No. 1589/2026) suspended industry appeals against the Ministry of Health decree of 29 December 2023 and referred the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Italian Constitutional Court.

If it were priced, a $20m swing factor on a $830m quarter — 2.4 points of reported growth, sitting outside the organic definition and therefore invisible to anyone anchoring on 'organic' — would appear in preview commentary as a bridge item, and it does not. The sign is genuinely two-sided, which is why the band straddles zero.

If the market had done that arithmetic, the 17 August release would have read as a mild negative revision to the reported quarter rather than as good news, and Flex-driven price targets would not still sit $20-26 against a $19.97 spot. The offset — and the reason this is only worth a point or so — is that the same fact makes Q2 commentary easy for management to spin.

text: Medtronic's April 2026 intrusion (ShinyHunters, unauthorised access 13-19 April 2026) resulted in notification of 3,834,294 individuals, with letters going out from late June into July 2026 — squarely inside MiniMed's fiscal Q1 — and several class actions already filed; exposed fields include Social Security numbers and health information. MiniMed filed its own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident on 2026-04-27 saying it was 'not aware of any compromises to the IT systems used by its business', but it has never quantified exposure, and the Q1 10-Q is the first periodic filing that must address it while MiniMed still runs on Medtronic IT under the separation arrangements.

If the market had attributed a material share of the remediation, indemnity and litigation exposure to MMED, you would see it in the pre-print tape and in a discount to the $20 IPO price, not a 20d gain.

This is worth little on its own, but it is the reason I do not read the skew as a directional statement, and confirming an absence at zero cost is the point.

BizLink (3665.TW), named in Credo's FY2026 10-K as the third-party manufacturer of its AEC products, printed accelerating record monthly revenue straight through Credo's fiscal Q1 (3 May - 1 Aug 2026): May NT$7.352bn (-0.4% MoM, +41.3% YoY), June NT$8.518bn (+15.9% MoM, +63.8% YoY), July NT$9.630bn (+13.1% MoM, +59.6% YoY, all-time high) — roughly +31% across the May-to-July span against a Credo revenue guide implying only +6.4% to +8.7% sequential.
why_not_priced: Taiwan-exchange monthly revenue filings are not carried in any US sell-side preview of CRDO — the Zacks, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com previews all frame the quarter off the company's own $465-475m guide and the ~$471.7m consensus with no channel data at all. If the market had made this read, the front-expiry 25-delta skew would not sit at +7.31 vol points to the put side, and the stock would not have surrendered the entire $283-to-$216 August move into a print whose sole named AEC manufacturer was printing back-to-back record months. The BizLink July figure is dated 5 August 2026 (year confirmed in the technews.tw URL path /2026/08/05/), i.e. after Credo last spoke on 1 June and inside the quarter being reported.

text: Credo filed no Item 2.02 8-K — indeed no 8-K of any kind — between 1 June and 1 September 2026, even though this quarter has the same ~31-day quarter-end-to-print gap (ended 1 Aug, prints 1 Sep) as fiscal Q3 2026 (ended 31 Jan, printed 2 Mar), when on 9 February 2026 it pre-announced preliminary revenue of $404-408m against prior guidance of $335-345m nine days after quarter end.
why_not_priced: No aggregator publishes the fact that a company did not file. The EDGAR 8-K list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001807794&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=20) shows the last 8-K as 2026-06-01, so under an identical calendar structure the company chose silence where it once chose to disclose a ~19%-above-guide quarter. That thins the fat right tail. If the market had drawn this inference, front-month ATM IV would not be 140.7% and the three-day straddle would not be pricing an 11.73% move; the option market is still paying for a Feb-9-style shock in either direction.

text: Both mechanisms that could crash this print were pre-committed by management on the 1 June call: the CFO guided Q2 FY27 sequential growth as 'mid single digits, between our Q1 guide, and you can expect something similar in our Q2 guide' (i.e. roughly $490-500m), and guided FY27 non-GAAP gross margin 'to be broadly consistent with fiscal year 2026 levels' — whereas the -14.81% reaction on 2 March 2026 was caused specifically by cutting the Q4 non-GAAP gross-margin guide to 64-66% from 68.6% reported, not by revenue.
why_not_priced: The previews in circulation (Seeking Alpha's '$600M optical revenue ramp in focus', Zacks' 'CRDO Bets on Optical Boom to Drive 80%+ Growth') frame the story as an H2 hockey stick and never state that the Q2 number is already pre-guided to mid-single-digit sequential — so a Q2 guide near $495m, which screens as a violent deceleration off 108-113% YoY growth, carries no new information. If the market had priced that, the 25-delta skew would not be +7.31 vol points put-side on a name whose put/call open interest ratio is only 0.81 and which has already round-tripped -24% from its 18 August level; the skew is paying for a guidance shock whose shape and margin floor were both put on the record three months ago.

Executive or CFO departure — Dan Fleming still listed as CFO, no Item 5.02 8-K since 29 October 2025

Non-cancellable purchase commitments and inventory as a forward indicator — Q1 FY27 10-Q is not filed yet, and the FY26 10-K notes were not retrievable through the fetch layer; inventory at $250.8m vs $90.0m is up 179% against revenue up 157%, which is unremarkable for a doubling business

DustPhotonics dilution or a hidden opex/interest-income step-up — the 1 June call already guided Q1 non-GAAP opex to $86-90m, FY27 opex +~50% YoY, and the $750m net cash outflow in Q1, and consensus $1.17 ties almost exactly to the guide midpoint, so there is no modelling gap

Evidence that a hyperscaler is insourcing AECs or designing copper out of next-gen racks — no dated primary source found; Marvell's 27 August call talked up CPO/NPO and 'end-to-end portfolio' but said nothing about AECs

Both of Dell's closest server-assembler comparables reported the overlapping April-June 2026 quarter in mid-August with massive margin upside in the teeth of the memory spike - Super Micro delivered 17.5% GAAP gross margin on 11 Aug against its own prior guidance of 8.2-8.4%, and Lenovo's ISG posted a record 9.1% operating margin on 13 Aug against a ~4.6% consensus - which is the direct empirical refutation of the 'the assembler eats the memory bill' thesis that Dell's own preview coverage says is the whole question for this print.
why_not_priced: The 31 Aug Motley Fool preview - the piece that defines the sell-side framing for this print, and which explicitly makes ISG operating margin versus Q1's 10.5% the pass/fail test - names no comparable at all, saying only that 'chip designers have spent recent weeks describing what those costs are doing to their margins'. If the comps' actual margin outcome were in the price, DELL would not be 10.8% off its 52-week high with a -5.58% 20-day run-up, Morgan Stanley would not be Equal-Weight at $434 and UBS Neutral at $455 against a $441.19 spot, and the stock would not have handed back the whole +10% it made on 13 Aug plus more over the following two weeks. The market saw this datapoint once and then un-priced it; the sell-side never wrote it down as a Dell read-across at all.

text: IDC's calendar-Q2 2026 PC data, covering two of the three months of Dell's fiscal Q2, shows the memory shortage working as a pricing-power event rather than a margin event for OEMs - shipments fell 4.9% to 68.2m units and Dell fell 5% to 9.3m while industry revenue rose, with comparable-line prices up 20-40% year over year and IDC stating vendors 'are pushing through price increases faster than demand is dropping'; Dell held share at 13.6%.
why_not_priced: The entire preview conversation on DELL is about ISG; CSG is roughly a third of revenue and is where memory inflation is proportionally most severe against a mid-single-digit segment margin, so a CSG print is the leg with the most room to surprise in either direction. The visible tell that it is unpriced is that the headline the market consumed from this data was 'PC shipments fall for the first time in two years' and 'Dell -5%', not the revenue and ASP mechanic underneath it - and Dell's own Q1 FY27 already showed CSG operating margin going the opposite way to the fear, up 280bp year over year to 8.0% (three months ended 1 May 2026, 10-Q). If the market had joined those two facts, the run-up into this print would not be negative and the coverage would be arguing about CSG, which it is not.

FuelCell's own careers site right now shows 61 of its 80 open requisitions at the Torrington cell plant and, critically, an entire third shift being staffed end-to-end -- Supervisor Tape Casting (Third Shift), Sheet Metal Supervisor (Third Shift), Warehouse Supervisor (Third Shift), Material Handler (Third Shift), QA Inspector Manufacturing (Third Shift), EH&S Specialist (Third Shift), Facility Tech (Third Shift), Janitor (Third Shift) and Security Officer (3rd Shift), plus a parallel second-shift set -- i.e. a 24/7 line being commissioned, not incremental backfill.
why_not_priced: Management explicitly declined to give a current annualised production rate on the 8 June call, so the only public number is the aspiration (500 MW/yr, $200-275m, 24 months). Nobody aggregates shift designations in job postings. If the market had this, the mid-August coverage would be arguing about output cadence and the $213m raise as pre-funded plant capex; instead the wire copy is 'dilution concerns tied to the $225m July offering' and rate-driven risk-off, and 25-delta puts would not be bid 11.6 vol points over calls on a name whose plant is hiring janitors and security guards for a third shift. Third-shift support functions are the cheapest possible tell that the shift is actually being run, because no one hires a 3am janitor speculatively.

text: Homer John Livingston III, who only became a FuelCell director on 19 May 2026, bought 26,343 shares in the open market on 16 July 2026 at a weighted-average $18.79 (about $495k, transaction code P, direct) -- an actual cash purchase at a company where every other recent insider line is a director-fee stock grant or a 10b5-1 sale.
why_not_priced: It was filed on 20 July into the middle of the sector de-rating and the stock has fallen another 11% since, so it plainly did not set the price; a market that had weighted it would not be paying an 11.6-point put skew nine days before the print. The signal is the contrast, and the contrast requires reading three separate accessions in the same week rather than a headline: the two Form 4s filed 16 July are zero-price director-fee deferred stock units (Livingston 833 units, Hansen 988 units) and the 6 July Form 4 is an EVP selling 2,500 shares at $28.71 under a plan adopted in January. A buy at $18.79 by a nine-week-old director is the only discretionary cash commitment in the file.

text: The Fit Energy CEPA's only alignment mechanism -- 12,000,000 warrant shares in three 4m tranches, each vesting only on FuelCell receiving a non-refundable deposit equal to 16% of the order value for the next 100 MW -- is struck at $26.44, now 58% above the $16.72 spot, and in the ten weeks since signing there has been no 8-K, no press release, no named data-centre site and no phase election; FuelCell's press-release feed shows nothing operational since 9 July, against management's own commitment to convert submitted proposals into contracted backlog 'within this fiscal year' (FY ends 31 October).
why_not_priced: The 54% drawdown from the 52-week high does price 'Fit optionality is worth less', which is why I size this small and negative-but-modest rather than large. What is not priced is the specific mechanism: only Phase 0 (30 MW) is committed, Phases 1-3 (350 MW) are at Fit's sole option, and the consideration FuelCell offered Fit for electing them is now deep out-of-the-money paper with a hard 24-month vesting cliff from 22 June 2026. If the market had modelled that, the sell-side previews would be framing 2 September as a Phase-1-election checkpoint rather than an EPS event, and there would be visible commentary on Fit Energy USA LP itself -- a Boca Raton vehicle whose named CEO, Joel Leonoff, comes from payments, not power, and which has issued nothing of its own since 24 June.

CXM's own five prior prints moved +5.96%, -10.00%, +3.05%, +6.05%, -3.03% (close before to close of the print day, all pre-open releases) and the sign is conditioned on the run-in: the only double-digit decline, 2025-09-03, was the print it entered at $8.60 near its 52-week high, which is the same setup as today at $7.94-8.21 after +22.6% in 20 days.
why_not_priced: The sealed baseline records history.n = 0 and options total open interest of 413 contracts with an ATM bid-ask 143% of mid, i.e. there is literally no market-visible statement of an expected move on this name and nobody is positioned for one. If this conditional base rate were in the price, a 62.7% ATM vol name two sessions from a print would have a two-sided chain and bid puts; instead the only thing in the price is a 20-day run-up that the IGV melt-up explains on its own. The baseline generator itself discarded all 21 prints on CIK 0001569345 as belonging to a predecessor entity, so the reaction history is not even available to whoever built the calendar row.

text: Sprinklr's FY27 non-GAAP operating income guide of $139-141m requires H2 operating income of ~$77-79m against H1 of ~$61.7m (Q1 actual $31.7m plus Q2 guide midpoint $30.0m) — a ~30% step-up in the quarterly run-rate that the CFO justified only as 'improve gradually in the second half of the year as we expect some efficiency gains' — and that FY OI guide had already been cut from $144-146m at the March print.
why_not_priced: This is guidance arithmetic across two press releases and a transcript, and only 8 analysts cover the name — stockanalysis.com records that their price targets were last updated 2026-06-04, when CXM closed at $5.38, with one refresh since. If the H2 bar were in the price, the average target would not still sit at $7.88 below a $7.99 spot with the stock at a 12-month high; the sell-side has simply not re-underwritten the FY27 OI ramp since the guide was cut, so a second cut lands into unrevised models rather than into pre-positioned ones.

text: The Q2 FY27 revenue guide implies professional services of only ~$20.5m (total $214-215m less subscription $193.5-194.5m) versus actual PS of $24.7m, $27.2m and $28.8m in the last three quarters, and Sprinklr beat its own implied PS guide by 25% in Q3 FY26 ($28.8m actual vs $23.0m implied) and 10% in Q1 FY27 ($24.7m vs $22.5m implied) — so a headline revenue beat of roughly 1.5-2.5% is mechanically likely, but at the -10% PS gross margin management guided it adds nothing to operating income.
why_not_priced: The wire carries 'Sprinklr poised to beat earnings estimates again' as an undifferentiated positive; what it does not carry is that the beat is structurally located in the one revenue line that runs a negative gross margin, so the headline and the margin move in opposite directions. If this were priced, the sell-side would model PS separately and the stock would not react to the total-revenue line — yet the 2026-06-03 print beat revenue, EPS and operating income and still closed down 3%, which is exactly what a market reading the total line and then the guide does.

text: In the Q1 FY27 10-Q geographic disaggregation, Americas revenue FELL to $112.9m from $117.6m (-4.0% YoY) while 'Other' jumped to $29.6m from $15.9m (+86%), so 48.6% of revenue is now outside the Americas versus 42.8% a year earlier and 44% for FY26 — Sprinklr's home market is contracting and every dollar of growth is coming from the regions where the Middle East disruption and FX sit.
why_not_priced: This table is in a 6MB 10-Q note; it is not in the earnings press release, it was not raised on the Q1 call, and no wire copy on the name mentions it. If the market had focused on a declining US base at ~51% of revenue, the story on the tape would be 'domestic decline offset by emerging-market wins', not 'AI transformation and improving renewals' — and a stock whose largest region shrinks does not close at a 12-month high on a 22.6% 20-day run without one analyst refreshing a target since 2026-06-04.

text: The Q1 FY27 10-Q discloses that 'our operations in the Middle East have been affected by the 2026 Iran conflict, including disruptions to our business activities in the region and inaccessibility, and potential loss, of certain customer data in connection with a third-party data center infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates' and warns of 'significant and unanticipated expenses... emergency data transfers, temporary changes to data processing locations, increased infrastructure costs' — and the conflict's targeting of Gulf data centres was still live in July 2026, i.e. across the whole of the quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026).
why_not_priced: Management framed this on the Q1 call as a discrete quarter event — 54 customers 'moved on the fly' out of a damaged Middle East environment to Ireland and '$3 million to $4 million of slip deals' — and the market treated it as behind them: CXM bottomed at $4.91 on 2026-06-25 and then rose 67% with no company news. If the market had carried it forward into Q2 it would not have re-rated the stock 67% while the same conflict was still striking Gulf data centres in July, and the unquantified infrastructure and remediation costs would show up in sell-side gross-margin estimates that have not been revised since 2026-06-04.

text: The scheduled termination date of Sprinklr's $125m variable-tenor accelerated share repurchase with Citibank is September 1, 2026 — today, the session before the print — after which the dealer's covering purchases (roughly $125m spread over ~115 sessions on a 2.76m-share ADV) stop, and only $75m of the $200m authorization remains through 15 March 2027.
why_not_priced: The termination date exists only in a 10-Q footnote: on the Q1 call management said only 'we repurchased 17.1 million shares' and '$75 million remaining', with no mention of the September 1 date or the pending final settlement, and no wire copy on the name mentions it. The baseline itself concedes that with no usable option chain 'what is priced' is INFERRED FROM THE RUN-UP — so a mechanical, price-insensitive buyer inside that run-up is precisely the contamination the baseline cannot see. If the market knew the bid ended today, the last four sessions would not have printed 3.2m/4.7m/4.2m/4.6m shares against a 1.7-2.4m ADV three weeks earlier on zero company news. The upper end of my band is real: with $502.5m of cash and $141.9m of FY26 free cash flow, a fresh or expanded authorisation announced with the print is the natural offset.

text: A reported 'August 4, 2026' Sprinklr layoff of 15%/500 staff turned out to be the February 2025 reduction: the CX Today source is dated 2025-02-07 (https://www.cxtoday.com/contact-center/sprinklr-slashes-15-of-staff-but-keeps-hiring-in-prioritized-areas/). Dead lead, dropped.
layoffs.fyi has no entry at all for Sprinklr (https://layoffs.fyi/company/sprinklr/); no state WARN filing for Sprinklr found for 2026.

A 'Wall Street projections for CXM Q2' piece on Nasdaq that search served as current is dated 2024-08-29 (consensus revenue $194.58m, i.e. FY25) — discarded as a relabelled article (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/insights-sprinklr-cxm-q2-wall-street-projections-key-metrics).

The Greenhouse board API 404s and sprinklr.com/careers/all-jobs/ 404s.
No federal contract award to Sprinklr found for 2026; the FedRAMP ATO material is from 2024.
No Sprinklr status-page incident record, app-store review trend, or customer-community thread found that bears on the May-July 2026 quarter.

Sprinklr's $125m accelerated share repurchase with Citibank has a stated scheduled termination date of September 1, 2026 - the last session before the print - so the dealer's programmatic buying of roughly 21m shares (about 6-7% of the 2.76m-share ADV every day since 11 March) ends exactly as the event begins; the stock's 54% advance from $5.32 on 1 July to $8.21 on 31 August came in near-daily 1-3% increments with no news gap, and CXM was quoted down 3.3% at $7.94 on 2026-09-01 itself, the ASR's termination date.
why_not_priced: The termination date lives in one sentence of a Q1 10-Q footnote ('The scheduled termination date is September 1, 2026 ... As of April 30, 2026, the ASR Agreement remained unsettled') and appears in no wire story, no preview and no analyst note; if the market had priced the withdrawal of the bid you would not see a 9-analyst average target of $7.88 sitting BELOW a $8.00 spot with nobody having refreshed since June, and you would not see the run-up delivered as a gapless daily grind - a fundamental re-rating on the Ribas board seat (17 Aug) or the Summer '26 release (15 Jul) would have produced a step, and in any case the run began on 1 July, weeks before both.

text: The quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026) was run without a Chief Revenue Officer for two of its three months: Scott Millard resigned effective 2025-11-11 after roughly seven weeks in the job, Tom Addis did not start until 2026-07-01, and SVP Global Sales Kevin Connolly left for NewRocket in the same window - so tomorrow's Q3 guide is the first ever set by a revenue chief with two months of tenure.

Petco's Q2 and FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes NO further IEEPA tariff refunds beyond the partial one received in May 2026, yet CBP's CAPE Phase 2 opened 29 June 2026 and BARK - a pet-products importer - booked a reconciliation line item literally labelled 'IEEPA Tariffs Phase II' worth $7.363M in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, which sits entirely inside Petco's 3 May - 1 Aug fiscal Q2.
why_not_priced: The sweep found a single $0.03 EPS estimate on this name - there is no sell-side machine tracking which CAPE phase disbursed when, and no WOOF note or wire item connects BARK's 6 August Phase-II disclosure to Petco's quarter. If it were priced, WOOF would not have fallen 6.9% in the week Evercore raised its target to $4 from $3.50 (31 Aug), and the June-3 sentence 'no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year' would be quoted in previews as an explicit upside option rather than ignored. Petco's CFO quantified the direct exposure at ~7% of total merchandise COGS sourced from China/Canada/Mexico for owned brands, i.e. roughly $200M of annual import cost, so the residual refund is plausibly high-single to low-double-digit millions against a $110-112M Q2 adjusted EBITDA guide. Risk to the finding: BARK excluded its refund from adjusted EBITDA, and Petco could do the same or book it in Q3 - hence the wide band.

text: Petco's FY2026 guide is pinned to 'fuel prices remain elevated at approximately those experienced in the first quarter' - fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr) averaged about $4.71/gal diesel on BTS monthlies ($3.72 / $4.92 / $5.50), fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) averaged about $5.20, and diesel was $5.599/gal on 31 Aug with US diesel cracks setting an all-time record above $106/bbl on 1 Sep and record-low seasonal distillate stocks going into heating season - leaving the stated H2 assumption roughly 19% below spot.
why_not_priced: Petco names fuel as one of only two quantified guidance assumptions, so it is material enough to move the FY $415-430M adjusted EBITDA range, yet no WOOF-specific coverage carries a diesel number. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be trading with two Buy-side target actions in the last two weeks and no preview flagging the assumption as stale; the run-up of -10.5% over 20 days is too small and too undifferentiated to be this. Fiscal Q2 fuel was already inside the Q2 guide (management said the May refund would be 'approximately offset by incremental tariffs and higher fuel costs'), so the live risk is the H2/FY guide, not the Q2 print - which is why the band is wide and the upper bound is only mildly positive.

text: The two freshest independent pet-category datapoints both landed on 5 August 2026, after Petco last spoke, and both improved with raised guidance - Central Garden & Pet's Pet segment organic net sales +2% for the quarter ended 27 June 2026 with FY non-GAAP EPS raised to '$2.85 or better' from '$2.70 or better', and Freshpet net sales +15.5% to $305.6M with FY net sales growth raised to 10-12% - while Chewy, the market's default category anchor, does not report until 9 September, a week AFTER Petco.

Central and Freshpet contradicted that in August and neither release mentions Petco, so the read-across was never written. If it were priced, Petco's Q2 net sales guide of 'up about 0.3%, in line with consensus' would be treated as a floor rather than a ceiling, and WOOF would not have drifted lower against two upgraded pet-category guides.

Only 6 analysts cover a $668M-cap name and the model has sat at $238-240M per quarter through a period when management raised the full-year revenue guide to $1,025-1,075M (implying a $256-269M quarterly average) and disclosed a +$50M data-centre step-up. If the market had reflected the building blocks, the estimate would have moved with the June guide instead of staying within $0.5M of the estimate that a $298.1M quarter beat by 25%, and Baird ($16) and Sidoti ($17) would not both still carry targets below the $18.71 spot. text: Every external datapoint bearing on Methode's two growth lines post-dates the 25 June guide: hyperscaler 2026 capex was raised across the board in late July (Amazon $200B to $220B, Alphabet $180-190B to $195-205B, Meta narrowed up), and GM raised its own FY26 EBIT guidance by $500M on 21 July while running Flint Assembly six days a week from June on heavy-duty pickup demand - while Methode's data-centre number is built only on existing vendor-managed busbar volume with the 800VDC rack architecture explicitly excluded from guidance by management.
why_not_priced: Hyperscaler capex itself is the most-covered fact in the market and I am not claiming it is unpriced. The unpriced part is the specific timing asymmetry in Methode's guide: management set the $130M data-centre number and the $72-82M EBITDA range on 25 June, before those raises, and said on the call that 'when we reference the future technology and the 800-volt architectures, none of that is in our guide.' That means the guide has one-sided slack and the print has no mechanism to falsify the 800VDC thesis that drove the Craig-Hallum initiation - the bear catalyst most people would expect here cannot actually occur at the guidance level this early. If the market had connected the two, the July capex raises would have moved MEI at the time; they did not - the stock only moved on 24 August on a boutique initiation, a month later.

text: Q4 FY26's headline was inflated by $22.5M of non-recurring customer recoveries recognised as revenue, so adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M on 24.2% gross margin sat on roughly $275.6M of underlying revenue and only single-digit-millions of underlying EBITDA; management said recovery activity is 'largely done' and excluded the remaining balance from FY27 guidance, so this print delivers the year's worst sequential optics - revenue down ~15% and EBITDA down sharply from Q4 - into a stock at a 52-week high.
why_not_priced: This one is mostly priced and I am filing it at residual size only, because the +14.23 vol points of 25-delta put skew is exactly what a market braced for a trough quarter after a recovery-inflated comp looks like. The residual that is not priced is the composition detail: the $22.5M is disclosed as revenue, not as an EBITDA add-back, so a reader working from adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M and a 24.2% gross margin will not see how thin the underlying run-rate was, and the ~45% sequential EBITDA decline that follows mechanically will read as deterioration rather than as arithmetic. This is compatible with finding 1 rather than contradicting it - a revenue beat alongside weak EBITDA is precisely what March 2026 printed, and the stock fell 12-15% on that combination.

text: Exactly one year ago Methode postponed this same fiscal quarter's release on the scheduled release day - 3 September 2025, having pre-announced 3 September on 21 August 2025 - gave no reason whatsoever in the reschedule notice, and the stock fell 11.4% the following session; it then reported six days later, on 9 September 2025, with a revenue beat ($240.5M vs $224.57M) and an EPS beat (-$0.22 vs -$0.40).
why_not_priced: No preview, no aggregator and no analyst note mentions it - the event simply does not appear in any of the three Q1 previews I read, and it is invisible to the baseline because the baseline's history is empty. It is a fiscal-Q1-specific close-process fragility with a documented 11.4% price consequence, and a repeat would be announced within hours of now. If the market carried it, the front-expiry chain would not be implying only a 7.4% event move on a name whose last three prints and pre-print notices produced -11.4%, -12 to -15% and +23.7%. I am sizing this as an expected value on a low-probability tail, not as a forecast that it recurs; the company filed no NT 10-Q and the 2025 outcome was benign.

Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M (9.0% margin) versus Q3 FY26's $7.3M (3.1% margin) is a $19.6M sequential jump that is almost exactly the ~$19M of one-time EV customer recoveries management said flowed through to earnings; ex-recoveries Q4 margin was ~2.9%, i.e. flat with Q3, and the FY27 guide of $72-82M adj EBITDA is therefore +47% to +67% off a recovery-adjusted FY26 base of ~$49M, not the +6% to +20% the headline $68.2M comparison implies.

The release is after tonight's close and the call is not until 08:00 ET tomorrow, so the first-session reaction is priced off the press release alone - which can contain the Q1 numbers and a guidance line, but structurally cannot contain the 800V rack-architecture narrative that management explicitly excluded from guidance and that the last four sessions have been buying. why_not_priced: This is a correction to how the sealed baseline reads rather than new news, and it has two offsetting legs that I am deliberately filing as one because they rest on a single fact - the July NXP rumour. Leg one (negative, dominant): a -20% 20-day run-up, -31.5% from the 52-week high and a 2.14 put/call open-interest ratio normally say 'expectations already cut, positioning defensive, bar low'. Here none of that is true - the drawdown is a mechanical premium unwind concentrated in the six sessions after 7 August, the pre-rumour price is essentially intact beta-adjusted, and the put-heavy open interest is more plausibly deal-related option residue than a fundamental bearish bet. So the standard 'beaten-down semi bounces on an in-line print' trade is not actually set up, and anyone sizing off the baseline's run-up field will over-weight it. Leg two (positive, smaller): the market is now pricing deal probability at roughly zero even though no source reports the talks dead, leaving a live low-probability, high-payoff tail - a signed merger agreement released alongside earnings, which does happen. If the market still carried any deal probability, the stock would not have round-tripped below the undisturbed close; if it were confident the talks were dead, there would be a story saying so, and there is not.

Consensus of a ($0.30) GAAP loss on 5 estimates bridges almost exactly off the $56-59m guide midpoint at face value, which is what you get when analysts take the guide and never open the footnote. So either the credit sits on top of the guide as an unguided ~$0.21/share benefit, or it is silently inside it and Q3 opex must step back up ~$9m - and management has said nothing that lets the market tell which. Had this been priced, at least one of the press release, the prepared remarks or the Q&A would have carried the words 'one-time' or 'credit', and none does.

text: Quanex's leverage cushion is thin (3.1x net-debt/LTM-EBITDA at 4/30/26 against a 3.25x covenant that tightened from 3.75x this fiscal year), and the strong Q3 2025 quarter ($70.3M adj EBITDA) rolls OUT of the LTM denominator this print while Q3 2026 price-cost recovery is by management's own account incomplete until Q4 - so the ratio can tick UP toward the covenant in Q3 before the Q4 improvement they are guiding to.
why_not_priced: The covenant step-down to 3.25x and the roll-off of a strong comp is arithmetic buried in the credit-agreement footnote and the LTM bridge; with one analyst covering the name, nobody is publicly modelling the quarter-by-quarter leverage path, so a Q3 ratio that brushes 3.2x-plus would be a surprise the flat-YoY consensus does not contemplate. If priced, the put skew would be positive (it is null) and puts would be bid rather than the chain being near-dead at 199 total OI.

text: Planet's own Q3 FY26 release states the NRO renewed its baseline EOCL contract for PlanetScope broad-area monitoring for $13.2M 'through June 2026' - so Planet's anchor US intelligence contract expired inside the quarter just reported, and no renewal has been announced anywhere in the June-September 2026 window even though Planet press-released two seven-figure European deals in that same window.
why_not_priced: The expiry date is buried in a highlights bullet of a nine-month-old press release, not in any calendar or estimate revision. Planet discloses US-government renewals inside earnings releases rather than as standalone PRs, so there is no wire item for the market to react to and no analyst note keyed to a June-2026 expiry. If this were priced there would be a visible bear note on US-government revenue continuity and the 25-delta skew would exist and be positive; the baseline reports no skew at all and a call-heavy 0.59 put/call open interest ratio.

text: FY27 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $0-10M against FY26 actual adjusted EBITDA of $15.5M - profitability guided DOWN while revenue is guided up ~41% - and the EBITDA range has stayed $0-10M through two upward revisions to both revenue ($415-440M to $425-441M) and gross margin (50-52% to 52-54%), which arithmetically requires roughly 30% opex growth; Planet's job board currently carries 114 open requisitions, overwhelmingly quota-bearing sales, pre-sales and customer-success roles in Berlin/Netherlands/UK.
why_not_priced: The wire framing for this print is 'path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven', which is inverted - Planet was already at $15.5M of adjusted EBITDA in FY26 and is guiding to at best $10M in FY27. If the market held the correct framing, a Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $0-5M would read as a year-on-year step down rather than as a breakeven milestone, previews would lead on the opex ramp, and the stock would not be quoted on a revenue-growth multiple. Nobody reconciles a raised gross-margin guide against an unchanged EBITDA guide, because the two live in different bullets of the same release.

text: The initial FY2027 guidance at this print will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10 — day 29 of his tenure and nine days after the fiscal year closed — as the fifth element of an eight-week C-suite reshuffle that includes an entirely unannounced departure: Matthew Echols ceased serving as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, disclosed only in an exit Form 4 filed 2026-08-27 with no press release and no 8-K.

If the market had focused on the Echols exit at all there would be a trade-press item; a search of Progressive Grocer, Shelby Report, Abasto and LinkedIn on 2026-09-04 still lists him in post, so the only public record of it is the Form 4.

text: UNFI's ~$330mm FY2026 free cash flow guide contains at least $40mm of one-off cyber insurance cash already banked through Q3 ($20mm in Q3 alone, 'included within Operating expenses'), which management itself strips out of adjusted EBITDA via a ($18mm) YTD 'Cybersecurity incident' reconciliation line — while the December 2025 framework anchors FCF at only '~$300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028'.
why_not_priced: It sits in a reconciliation footnote, not the headline, and it is internally inconsistent in UNFI's own favour: the same $40mm is excluded from the metric the company markets (adjusted EBITDA) and included in the metric the deleveraging story runs on (FCF). The consequence is arithmetic — an FY27 FCF guide anchored on the company's own ~$300mm framework prints below FY26's ~$330mm, and headline 'FCF guided down' is what a two-analyst tape reacts to. If this were priced you would see the FY26 FCF number quoted ex-insurance in previews; it is quoted at $330mm flat.

text: The Q4 bar the wire will print at 6:30am - $7.6bn revenue, $0.62 adjusted EPS - is asymmetric against UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide: $31.1-31.3bn sales less $23.51bn of 39-week actuals implies Q4 sales of $7.59-7.79bn, so $7.6bn sits at the floor of the guided band, whereas $2.40-2.60 adjusted EPS less $1.95 YTD implies Q4 of $0.45-0.65 and $0.62 sits at the ~85th percentile.
why_not_priced: This is the exact inverse of the Q3 setup, where the Street's $7.96bn revenue estimate sat roughly $260m above the guide-implied ~$7.7bn and the stock fell 10.28% on a revenue miss with in-line EPS and +16.6% EBITDA. If the market had absorbed the lesson symmetrically, the previews would be flagging that the revenue bar has now been set below the company's own floor; instead they simply reprint $7.6bn/-1.6% with no guidance bridge. The two aggregators do not even agree - the FY-level consensus of $31.20bn implies $7.69bn for Q4, $90m above the quarterly consensus being quoted.

text: The first FY27 guide has to be set against a fuel base far above FY26's with only partial hedging, and UNFI's own multi-year frame gives it cover to guide flat: EIA weekly diesel was $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 versus $3.708 a year earlier (+51%), the fiscal-Q1-to-date August average is $5.46 versus $3.74 (+46%), and against FY24 adjusted EBITDA of $518m the published "low-double-digit average annual Adjusted EBITDA growth from FY24 to FY27" target is satisfied by FY27 of roughly $690-730m - i.e. flat to +5% on the FY26 guide midpoint of $695m - even though the longer-term algorithm management talks to is high-single-digit EBITDA growth.
why_not_priced: Partly priced - the -6.6% twenty-day drift coincides with the August diesel run - which is why I have haircut it. What is not priced is the target arithmetic: nobody has published the FY24 $518m base against the FY24-FY27 CAGR target to show that management's headline multi-year promise is already met by a flat FY27, so the Street's FY27 models anchor on the high-single-digit algorithm (~$750m) rather than on the ~$700m the stated target actually obliges. If that had been done, the sell-side FY27 EBITDA distribution would be visibly bimodal and the previews would lead with FY27 rather than with Q4 revenue.

If the profit trajectory (108.2 -> 140.2 -> 158.4 -> 162.1 in 2025, then 98.4 in Q1 2026) were priced, the stock would not be running +5.7% in the five sessions into the print off its 52-week low; you would see it drifting down into the date, and the June print would have been a down day, not a +2.3% day.

text: Waterdrop's current US$50m share repurchase authorisation runs 'during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026' — expiring the day AFTER this 2026-09-08 print — and it has been almost unused: cumulative repurchases went from approximately US$109.0m (55.7m ADSs) at 2025-08-31 to approximately US$120.1m (61.8m ADSs) at 2026-05-31, so roughly US$11m of the US$50m was spent in nine months; the company has launched a new programme every September for five straight years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and announced the 2025 one inside the Q2 earnings release itself, and its semi-annual dividend's second-half tranche has likewise been declared with the September release (ex-dates 2024-10-11 and 2025-10-10), where US$0.03 per ADS is now 2.86% of a US$1.0495 spot versus roughly 1.5% a year ago.
why_not_priced: The 2026-09-09 expiry date exists only inside a twelve-month-old 6-K exhibit; no aggregator carries buyback authorisation expiries, and with no options market there is no vehicle in which anyone could have expressed a view on a one-day-later expiry. Yield trackers do show the dividend (dividend.com/stockanalysis show ~5.5%), so the dividend's EXISTENCE is priced — what is not re-marked anywhere is that the same absolute US$0.03 per ADS is now nearly twice its former size relative to a halved share price, and that the buyback has been dormant enough (approximately US$41k/day) that the 'large buyback' framing overstates any standing bid. If the September renewal were priced you would see the run-up concentrated in the days after 2026-08-25 when the date was announced rather than the broad +4.95% 20-day drift the baseline reports.

text: China's eight financial and internet regulators jointly issued the Administrative Measures for Online Marketing of Financial Products on 2026-04-24, effective 2026-09-30 — 22 days after this print — whose Article 20 bars third-party internet platforms (defined as sites and apps 'not self-operated by a financial institution') from intervening or covertly intervening in sales-contract signing, fund transfer or suitability assessment, and from conducting interactive consultation with consumers about financial products, which puts a hard compliance date on the traffic architecture behind Waterdrop's insurance marketplace and its non-licensed Waterdrop Medical Crowdfunding funnel.
why_not_priced: There is no English-language coverage connecting WDH to these Measures at all — searches for Waterdrop plus the rule return only the earnings-date press release. EDGAR full-text search for the Chinese term returns zero Waterdrop documents, so the FY2025 20-F filed 2026-04-28 (four days after issuance) does not name it. With no options and effectively no sell-side, there is no preview note in which a compliance date twenty-two days out could have been raised. If it were priced, the stock would have broken on 2026-04-24; instead the 2026-04/2026-06 tape shows no single-day dislocation and the June print was a positive reaction. I size it near zero and two-sided on purpose: the rule plausibly HELPS a licensed self-operated broker by forcing unlicensed traffic platforms to hand users off, which is Waterdrop's own model — the risk is that management is asked to quantify it on the 8:00 ET call and cannot.

The US airline earnings cycle broke inside ABM's fiscal Q3 (1 May - 31 July 2026) and after ABM last guided: American cut FY26 guidance to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 range and guided Q3 to an adjusted loss of $0.10-$0.70, Southwest cut FY26 EPS to $3.25-$4.25 and trimmed capacity growth to ~1.5%, and Alaska suspended guidance and cut May and June capacity, on jet fuel of $3.65-$4.50/gal — while ABM's Aviation segment operating margin had already collapsed to 5.25% in Q2 FY26 ($16.3M profit on $310.8M revenue) from 6.34% a year earlier, and ABM runs 1,000+ conventionally fuelled shuttle buses and 2,000+ parking locations on largely fixed-price contracts.
why_not_priced: ABM's wire narrative is office-return, eMobility and data centres — Aviation is covered as the 19.5%-growth good-news segment, not as a fuel-shock exposure. If the market had transferred the airline shock, ABM would have de-rated with airline-supplier names through June and July instead of sitting 4.7% off its 52-week high with a -3.1% 20-day run-up; there would be a positive 25-delta skew instead of no skew at all, and there would be more than 93 contracts of total open interest in the front expiry. Five analysts and a consensus target essentially at spot mean nobody has published the segment arithmetic: Aviation is ~13.6% of revenue but only ~9.8% of segment operating profit, so a 50bp margin miss plus a 200bp growth deceleration is ~$4-5M of profit, roughly $0.05 of adjusted EPS on a ~$1.00 quarter, which is exactly the size of miss this name has reacted 6-9% to.

why_not_priced: The 2026-08-04 release that triggered the re-rating quoted 'approximately US$130 million' of digital asset holdings as of 2026-08-03 with no mention of pledges, and the CEO's quote framed the whole treasury as unrecognised value ('market value does not fully reflect the value of our digital asset holdings'). The stock is +69.8% over 20 days on that framing. If the market had netted off the 1,005 pledged/locked coins it would be comparing a ~US$64m free treasury (at ~US$80k BTC) against a ~US$250m market cap, not a US$130m one, and the asset-backing argument that carried the tape from ~0.21 to 0.3634 would not survive that arithmetic. Corroborating flow arithmetic from a separate document set: Canaan mined 90 + 90 + 64 BTC in Apr/May/Jun and received 3 + 24 BTC from customers, i.e. at least 271 coins in, yet treasury rose only from 1,807.6 to 1,915 (+107) - so roughly 160 coins were liquidated inside Q2 to fund operations, and a further ~44 in July (46 mined, treasury 1,915 to 1,917).

If the market had focused on this, the coverage would be arguing about whether Q3 guidance can exceed the US$35-45m Q2 guide at all, rather than treating the Q2 print as a floor. The Jun-30 contract-liability balance in Tuesday's release is the number that settles it, and orders won only after BTC recovered in August would land at 2026-09-30, i.e. not in this filing.

The consequence is that Q2's mining revenue line will read as a structural collapse (64 BTC in June versus 90 in each of April and May) when the July filing already shows the fleet back at 100% utilisation, which is exactly the mitigant management will lead the 8:00 ET call with. This is the one leg of my set that cuts with the run-up rather than against it, and I have kept it small because the +69.8% tape has plainly absorbed some of the operational recovery already.

why_not_priced: If the street had marked to guidance, the Q2 consensus row would sit inside $35-45m and the FY2026 line would not still read $269.23m with a $1.72 average target and a Strong Buy consensus on a stock at $0.35. Instead the aggregators carry a Q2 number 20-58% above what the company itself told the market on 19 May and an FY number that implicitly assumes an H2 doubling; the wire copy on 8 September will therefore compute a 30-45% revenue shortfall against a stale base regardless of execution, and the +69.8% 20-day run-up shows the tape has been trading BTC beta, not estimate revisions. The auto-published 'earnings missed' article five days ahead of the print is the tell that even the data vendors have a Q2 number in the feed that the equity has not repriced for.

text: The liquidity line is the print's real unknown: cash fell from $80.8m at 2025-12-31 to $43.5m at 2026-03-31 (a $37.3m burn in one quarter) against $106.4m of current liabilities and $21.1m of loans due inside a year, 905 of 1,871 bitcoins were pledged as collateral for $54.5m of secured term loans, and Q2 revenue was guided 30-45% lower than Q1 — so the 30-June balance sheet, struck with BTC at $58,504 on 2026-06-30 (BTC's worst quarter in years, -34% YTD), is where the market first sees how little unencumbered liquidity is left behind the '$130m treasury' headline.
why_not_priced: If the market were pricing the cash line, a stock would not double in August on a treasury-value argument that quotes gross digital assets and ignores that 48% of the bitcoin is pledged and that $54.5m of secured loans sit against it. The August coverage that drove the move cited the $130m/$146.1m gross treasury and the March-31 cash figure; nobody has a June-30 cash number, and there is no live option chain and no put skew to show anyone hedging the possibility that it is materially below $43.5m. Canaan also has a $270m at-the-market sales agreement live since 2025-11-04 that requires no per-sale 424 filing, so issuance into the August rally is invisible until this print — and today's -11.0% session (prev close $0.3933, last $0.3501) on no filing and no press release is consistent with supply rather than news.

text: The stated trigger for the crypto-funded buyback has been extinguished by the rally it helped cause: on 2026-08-04 Canaan justified monetising digital assets by saying it was 'trading below the combined value of its digital assets holdings and its cash and cash equivalents as reported on March 31, 2026' ($130m treasury as of 3 August plus $43.5m cash = $173.5m, against a $144.7m market cap on 6 August), but after a 108.8% August the market cap is $261.0m while the treasury of 1,917 BTC and 3,952 ETH is worth roughly $165m at BTC ~$81.0k and ETH ~$2.4-2.5k — so on the company's own yardstick the stock now trades at roughly a 25% premium rather than a 17% discount, and the repurchase authorisation expires 2026-12-12.
why_not_priced: If the market had done this arithmetic it would not be paying a premium to a metric the company published as a discount, and the 20-day run-up would not be +69.8%. Canaan has never disclosed a repurchase figure since the ~$2m executed by 19 May — the 4 August release and the 17 August production 6-K both cite the authorisation and give no amount — so the market is long a 'the company is buying' story with no execution data. The 8 September release is the first venue where that number appears, and because the company's own stated condition for buying (trading below treasury plus cash) stopped holding somewhere in mid-August, a thin or zero repurchase disclosure is the base case and removes the prop under the August move.

text: The Nasdaq minimum-bid arithmetic is now impossible without a capital-structure action: the ADS must close at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days by 2027-01-11, which from $0.3501 is +186%, so an ADS ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares) has to be noticed to holders around November to be effective in time — and the 8 September call is the first scheduled management appearance since the deadline was granted.
why_not_priced: The deadline itself is in the wire, but the market is treating a stock that doubled as having escaped the problem when $1.00 is still nearly a triple away and only ~90 trading days remain. If it were priced there would be visible demand for downside protection into the ratio-change window; instead the option chain has 6,882 contracts of total open interest and a 0.03 put/call open-interest ratio, i.e. essentially nobody is short this. Canaan has already run the standard pre-reverse-split sequence — it transferred to the Nasdaq Capital Market on 2026-07-06 specifically to qualify for the second 180 days — so the remaining step is the ratio change, and reverse splits in this cohort are reliably sold.

A fiscal-year print with a live 8:00 ET call is the natural venue for either an offering or a share-consolidation intention, and either would land on an audience that has not read the July filings.

text: The $5m buyback that caused a +105% single-day move when announced on 2025-08-28/30 was 88% unused when it expired: the 2026-08-28 6-K discloses only about 518,063 Class A shares repurchased for roughly $600,000 (an average near $1.16), meaning the company stopped buying entirely as the stock fell from ~$1.16 to a 52-week low near $0.67, and then extended the same authorisation unchanged to 2027-08-28.
why_not_priced: The extension was disclosed only on a 6-K with no accompanying press release I can find, and it moved the stock +0.11% on 66,901 shares - whereas the original announcement of the identical programme moved it +105% on ~46m shares. The market has therefore priced the headline 'buyback' twice and the execution zero times; if it had read the execution it would treat the extension as neutral-to-negative optics rather than support, and the 5-day run-up of +5.77% into the print would not be there. It also sits awkwardly against an effective $200m shelf: a company simultaneously authorising repurchases it does not make and registering securities 4.5x its market cap.

text: The baseline's 20-day average volume of 405,662 shares is essentially one session: GMHS traded 7,142,358 shares on 2026-08-31 (+16.51%) with no company filing or press release on or around that date, while the surrounding sessions traded 6,192 (2026-08-13), 19,279 (2026-08-11), 22,908 (2026-08-12), 35,144 (2026-08-27) and 66,901 (2026-08-28) shares - so the true book into this print is tens of thousands of shares a day, and the +16.5% spike has already bled off across four consecutive down days to $0.77.
why_not_priced: This is a dispersion finding, not a directional one, and it says the baseline's expected_move_pct of 4.19% is the wrong width. With no options market there is no implied move to correct it, and the 20-day ADV that would normally warn a reader about liquidity has been inflated ~8x by a single unexplained session. If the market were pricing this correctly the name would carry a visible illiquidity discount and a much wider historic reaction distribution than the 4.19% median the baseline reports; instead one 17x-volume day is being read as normal turnover. Practically: a print-day order of ordinary institutional size cannot be filled without moving GMHS by a large multiple of 4.19% in whichever direction it arrives.
