BIOX's Nasdaq 180-day minimum-bid-price compliance period expires TODAY, 2026-09-14 - the same session the FY26 results are due - and at $0.4350 compliance is arithmetically impossible, so within days the company must disclose either a transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market with a written commitment to cure (in practice a reverse split) or a Staff delisting determination; it has no shareholder authority for a split, its 2026-01-30 AGM agenda carried only FY2025 accounts, four directors and the auditor, and no EGM has been noticed.
why_not_priced: A known, dated, binary listing deadline should leave fingerprints and leaves none: run_up_20d is -4.05% and run_up_5d -0.74% (no drift into the date), short interest is 913,482 shares = 2.03% of float as of 2026-09-09, and the entire option chain is 2,023 contracts of open interest with a put/call OI ratio of 0.01 and no two-sided ATM market. Nobody has bought a put, shorted a share, or sold into it. If the market had focused on this you would see a bid for downside protection and a visible pre-deadline slide, as sub-$1 names routinely show in the fortnight before a compliance expiry. I checked the eligibility arithmetic myself rather than assuming the worst: total equity was $95.7m and MVPHS is roughly $18-24m, so BIOX does clear the Nasdaq Capital Market Equity Standard ($5m equity, $15m MVPHS) and a second 180 days is genuinely available - which is why the band runs positive at the top. The negative centre is that the cure it must commit to is a reverse split on a $27.6m equity, announced into the same release as a going-concern year.

text: The New York Supreme Court granted Jasper Lake partial summary judgment ON LIABILITY on 2026-06-16 - fourteen days before the 2026-06-30 fiscal year end - finding multiple Events of Default, valid acceleration, and liability of both the company and its guarantors, while striking Bioceres' proposed counterclaims as contractually waived; damages, default interest, contractual premiums, fees and the deficiency accounting on the $107.1m claim all remain open, so the FY26 audited accounts must now measure a liability that was a contingency at the last balance sheet date, against parent-attributable equity that has already fallen from $265.4m to $67.7m in nine months.
why_not_priced: The disclosure exists but nothing has processed its accounting consequence. The stock moved +1.88% on the 2026-06-22 filing date, the calendar row carries no consensus EPS for this name at all, and there has been an eleven-week total news blackout between 2026-06-22 and the 2026-09-09 call notice - so no analyst has published a number for the provision and no one has to be surprised out of one. If the market had focused on it, a name whose total equity went $295.2m -> $106.6m -> $95.7m over three quarters while carrying an adjudicated default on $108.3m of already-current debt would not be sitting at a flat 20-day tape; you would see the equity-stub repricing that normally precedes a distressed FY print. The incremental item is not the principal (already on balance sheet as short-term debt) but the default-interest and make-whole layer plus the deficiency, now determined rather than disputed, and the loss of the counterclaim offset.

Neither happened, so what is actually priced is nothing, and the unpriced content is the inference the sequencing carries - a company puts a funding headline out hours before a print when it knows the balance sheet in that print needs cover. The range is wide and crosses zero because a facility validated with a named, checkable lender on the 17:00 call is genuinely good news the market has assigned zero value to.

It is not: if the transaction is still pending when the H1 statements are authorised for issue, the funding actually committed at that date is only ~EUR 12-13m of June-30 cash plus EUR 27.6m of net placement proceeds, i.e. ~EUR 40m against a burn that ran EUR 19.4m in Q1-2026 alone -- under twelve months, which is the specific condition that forces a going-concern material-uncertainty disclosure in a French semi-annual report reviewed by the statutory auditors. Nobody is modelling a going-concern paragraph on a stock whose last five weeks of coverage read 'funded to Q1 2028'; if they were, the 11 Aug Leerink upgrade to Outperform would have carried the condition and the stock would not have closed the gap to the EUR 1.70 placement price. This is genuinely two-sided: if the release instead announces the closing, that is a positive, which is why the band is wide and crosses zero.

Lennar's own full-year target of 'approximately 82,000 to 83,000 homes' arithmetically requires a Q4 of 23,118-25,118 deliveries (Q1 16,863 + Q2 20,519 = 37,382; Q3 guided 20,500-21,500), i.e. +0.4% to +9.0% against the 23,034 of Q4 FY25 which was itself the largest delivery quarter in company history, at a moment when new orders are guided down 4-9% year over year against the 23,004 comp.
why_not_priced: The sell side has taken the guide at face value rather than discounting it: FY2026 consensus revenue is $32.47bn (19 analysts, S&P Global, pulled 2026-09-16), only -5.0% on a fiscal 2025 that delivered 82,583 homes, and Q3 consensus revenue of $8.33bn sits exactly on the guide midpoint (Zacks' own model is 21,181 units at $377,230). If a Q4 cut were priced, FY26 consensus revenue would already sit a percent or two below the company's number, the average price target would not be $84.92 (+6% to spot), and the 25-delta skew would be put-bid rather than -0.77. Lennar has already walked this number from 'approximately 85,000' (2025-12-16) to 82,000-83,000 (2026-06-11) without consensus moving below it.

text: Lennar has printed at or below the bottom of its own guided ranges for two consecutive quarters: Q1 FY26 delivered 16,863 homes against a guide of 17,000-18,000 (below the range entirely) with gross margin 15.2% against a guided 15.0-16.0%, and Q2 FY26 gross margin was 15.6% against a guided 15.5-16.0% — so the Q3 guide of 'approximately 16%' more plausibly prints 15.5-15.8%.
why_not_priced: Nobody publishes a builder's guide-to-actual hit rate, and consensus is modelling the midpoint, not the floor: Zacks' Q3 model is 21,181 deliveries at $377,230 ASP — dead centre of the guided bands — and the consensus EPS has drifted only from $1.31 to $1.29 in the past week. If the market had priced the pattern, consensus would sit a nickel or more below the guide-midpoint arithmetic rather than on it. On roughly 21,000 homes at ~$377k, each 30bp of gross margin is about $24m pre-tax, near $0.07 a share, or 5% of the $1.29 consensus per 30bp.

If that were priced, the two covering analysts would not still carry an average $25.50 target (+91% on a $13.375 spot) with no cut since the guide was narrowed on 2026-05-13, and the 25-delta skew would not be -11.04 vol points with 'upside paid' into a company that has fallen on 5 of its last 6 prints. Note the specific tail: because the FY26 exit rate makes any growth guide hard to defend, the company may decline to guide FY27 at all, and a withheld guide is read as a cut.

text: The FY26 10-K discloses that the Global Retail reporting unit's fair value exceeded carrying value by just 1.1%, International Contract by 3.1%, and the Muuto and Knoll indefinite-lived trade names by 2.1% and 6.8% - cushions thin enough that the company says 'relatively modest adverse changes' in projected revenue growth or margin would produce material impairment charges, and MillerKnoll has form for taking interim impairments mid-year when performance disappoints.
why_not_priced: A 1.1% cushion is a critical-audit-matter footnote in a long 10-K filed in July on a three-analyst name; no aggregator carries reporting-unit cushion percentages and no preview mentions it. If it were priced, the forward PE would not be 10.0 with two of three analysts at a $35 target - a 69% upside target is not what a book carrying a near-zero goodwill cushion on 30% of revenue looks like.

The two peer prints that re-rated AZO both stopped measuring before AZO's quarter did: Advance Auto Parts' Q2 (12 weeks, quarter beginning after its Q1 ended 2026-04-25, so ending mid-July) reported comp -0.5% on 2026-08-20 and took AZO down 4% that day, but AZO's Q4 runs to 2026-08-29 and the only direct peer datapoint that covers July says demand stepped UP - O'Reilly on 2026-08-07: 'we did not realize the normal ramp up in demand for certain hot-weather-related categories' in June, then 'We have definitely seen summer take hold across our markets in July' with a 'step-up in sales results to start the third quarter,' particularly hot-weather categories - and NOAA has since recorded summer 2026 as the warmest in the 132-year US record (+3.0F) with August 2026 the warmest August on record, against AZO management's stated Q4 planning assumption of 'normal summer weather'.
why_not_priced: The price shows the market took the opposite read and took it on a stale window: AZO fell 4% to $2,961 on 2026-08-20 explicitly on AAP's DIY miss (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/20/advance-auto-parts-plunges-21-as-revenue-miss-overshadows-earnings-beat-autozone-falls-4-oreilly-automotive-slips/) and has since made a new 52-week low with TD Cowen, Oppenheimer and Citi all cutting targets into the print. If the market had weighted ORLY's July step-up and the record-hot August that sit inside AZO's quarter and outside AAP's, AZO would not be marking to AAP's mid-July four weeks, the sell-side targets would not be falling in the week the NOAA record was published, and the run-up would not be -4.75% over five sessions.

text: AZO's LIFO reserve has been built entirely by tariff inflation - the 10-Q states 'Due to price changes on the Company's merchandise purchases, primarily due to inflation driven by tariffs, the Company's LIFO credit reserve balance was $260.0 million at May 9, 2026, and $83.0 million at August 30, 2025' - and Q4 FY26 carries the easiest LIFO comp of the year (guided ~$30m charge, 45bp, against an actual $80m charge / 128bp in Q4 FY25), with upside to a credit if supplier pass-back of IEEPA refunds lowers replacement cost in the May-August window, which is the exact line the stock has been sold on for three consecutive quarters.
why_not_priced: Only the delta to the guide is unpriced and I say so: the $30m Q4 charge was guided on the 2026-05-26 call, so the +83bp YoY improvement is inside what the company already told the market to expect and is a reported-quarter item. What is not in any preview I could find is that the reserve is now $260m built from tariff inflation that the Supreme Court voided on 2026-02-20, and that peer retailers are already booking the reversal - AAP took $26m of tariff refunds worth 130bp of gross margin in its July quarter, Target applied $685m of $730m of refunds to reduce COGS, and ORLY says it is negotiating supplier sharing of refunds. If the market had priced a possible LIFO credit rather than the guided charge, the sell-side gross-margin cuts into this print would not be running the other way.

text: The FY2026 10-K, due roughly late October 2026, is where the full-year LIFO reserve roll-forward and any IEEPA tariff refund or gain-contingency disclosure will appear in primary form; CBP's CAPE liquidation process was still running at ~$128.7bn of accepted refunds as of 2026-07-31, so supplier pass-back to AZO continues to accrue after this print.

A direct IEEPA tariff refund receivable or gain contingency in AZO's own filings - the Q3 FY26 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/866787/000110465926073525/azo-20260509x10q.htm) carries no IEEPA, refund, customs or gain-contingency language at all, and AZO's model is supplier-as-importer-of-record like ORLY's, so there is no AAP-style direct refund line to find here

What IS visible is the skew at -11.51 (calls bid), which says the direction is at least partly paid for; that is exactly why this is 0.7 and not 2.5. The genuinely unpriced piece is narrow: consensus wire copy still describes the runway question as open (the sweep brief itself framed 'the gap between runway and a commercial launch' as the edge), when the 424B5 answered it as Q2 2029 eleven weeks ago.

text: The EMA MAA for obefazimod, guided for the second half of 2026 contingent on positive ABTECT maintenance data, has been absent from Abivax's own 'Anticipated Key Milestones' list in every release since that condition was met - the 2026-06-01 maintenance topline 6-K mentions no EMA, MAA, European marketing authorization or European regulatory pathway at all, and the 2026-06-29 list carries only three items (H1 results, NDA Q4 2026, ENHANCE-CD mid-2027).

The wire copy is uniformly 'NDA Q4 2026' with no EU line. H2 2026 has fourteen weeks left and tonight's release is the natural place for the milestone to be reinstated or formally deferred; a deferral to 2027 is a real, if small, NPV item that nobody is carrying.

text: The H1 2026 balance sheet is dated 30 June 2026 and therefore predates the 6 July closing of the $920m offering, so the headline cash figure will be roughly EUR 425-440m - visibly DOWN from the EUR 491.6m reported at 31 March - and the half-year loss per ADS should land near $1.45-1.55 against the $1.08 aggregator bar.
why_not_priced: Not so much unpriced as mechanically mis-scrapable: the period-end date falls five days before the financing closed, so headline algorithms and any reader anchored on the post-deal cash pile will see a 12% sequential cash decline and an EPS number well wide of the one aggregator print that exists. If the market had this right you would see previews distinguishing the 30 June balance sheet from the pro-forma; the one preview I found simply repeats '$1.08 loss on $1.86m revenue'. The effect is almost certainly a first-hour artefact that reverses before the exit, which is why it is -0.2 and not larger.

German new-registration data published by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt shows Wohnmobile down 15.7% in July 2026 and down 21.4% in August 2026 - a two-month collapse in Erwin Hymer's home market against a January-July cumulative of only -3.3% - while Thor's European segment was still shipping +4.2% units and +11.8% net sales in the February-April quarter with backlog up just 1.0%.
why_not_priced: The number is a single line item ('-21,4 %/1,9 %') inside a German-language KBA passenger-car press release published on 2026-09-03, eighteen days before this print. Every English-language THO preview I found anchors on RVIA wholesale and SSI retail, which are North American series; BMO's pre-print estimate cut was explicitly on 'softer retail and shipment trends' in the RV sector, i.e. the US data. The publicly circulating European datapoint is CIVD's seven-month figure of -3.0% overall and -3.3% for motor caravans, which is an order of magnitude milder than what July and August actually did, and CIVD's own Caravan Salon messaging in early September was that the industry 'expects recovery once the economic situation improves'. If the market had this, Thor's European segment - the leg that has grown net sales double digits for three straight quarters and carries ~38% of revenue - would be the thing preview notes name, and it is not. Net of the rest of the company [sizing note removed]: North America is ~62% of revenue and my read there is mildly positive, Thor Europe is taking share (24.4%, up), European backlog is +1.0% rather than falling, and the euro is roughly 3-4% stronger year on year (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/hist/dat00_eu.htm), so the reported European quarter can still be up in dollars. That is why this is filed as a guidance finding about FY27 European wholesale and not as a reported-quarter finding, and why it is sized -2.0 rather than the -4.5 the retail number alone would suggest. Caveat I am carrying explicitly: KBA's 'Wohnmobile' is a Pkw sub-category and is narrower than CIVD's 'Reisemobile', so the two series are not identical in definition.

text: Consensus Q4 revenue of $2.17-2.20bn requires Thor to print at or above the very top of its own unchanged FY26 guide: nine-month net sales are $7.297bn against a $9.0-9.5bn full-year range, so consensus sits at the 94th percentile of the guide while consensus EPS of $0.91-0.97 sits mid-range against the $0.71-1.21 the same guide implies.
why_not_priced: This is arithmetic off two primary documents that nobody publishes in the preview: the guide and the nine-month actuals are in the Q3 8-K, the consensus is on the wire, and the join is not. If the market had done the join, the published revenue consensus would sit near $1.95bn (the guide midpoint) rather than $2.17bn, and the revenue line would be the one the previews flagged as at-risk rather than the EPS line. What stops me sizing this larger, and I am resolving rather than leaving the contradiction to be added by the sum [sizing note removed]: a bottom-up cross-check from RVIA monthly shipments over May-July 2026 (industry -14.7%, towables ~-15.3%, motorhomes ~-10.4%) applied to Q4 FY25 segment revenue of $888.7m / $557.4m / $923.1m lands at roughly $2.15bn, essentially at consensus, while backlog-conversion off the 30 April 2026 segment backlogs (-39.1% / -13.3% / +1.0%) lands at roughly $1.96bn, essentially at the guide midpoint. The two methods bracket $1.96-2.15bn, so my honest point estimate is about $2.09bn, ~3.5% below the bar - a real but small miss, and a miss that lands inside a range the company already guided to, which [sizing note removed].

text: On 2026-09-10, twelve days before this print, Thor abandoned the decentralised operating model it has run for decades and put all North American RV operations under a single president and a single CFO, with the stated objective of 'drive out costs within the Company to strengthen our earnings profile' and benefits on an 'accelerated timeline' relative to the two-group structure announced earlier.
why_not_priced: The release was filed as a leadership-change announcement and the market read it as personnel: the stock is -5.38% over the five sessions to the seal and made a new leg toward its 52-week low after it. What the document actually contains is a structural reorganisation of a famously decentralised manufacturer with an explicit margin objective and no number attached, arriving twelve days before the one print of the year at which this company sets full-year guidance. If the market had priced it you would expect the pre-print drift to be positive rather than -5.38%, and you would expect at least one of the three pre-print analyst actions I could find (BofA target $96 to $86 on 2026-09-21, BMO estimate cuts, Wall Street Zen to Sell on 2026-09-20) to frame FY27 around a cost programme rather than around 'softer retail and shipment trends'. The inference I am making - that the FY27 guide arrives with a quantified structural-savings element - is an inference and not a disclosed number, which is why this is +1.5 and not larger.

text: Camping World, Thor's largest customer and holder of record US new-unit share above 29%, exited its June 2026 quarter with new vehicles on the lot down ~17% year on year in units (dollars down only ~5%), prior-model-year exposure on new RVs near 1% against over 6% a year earlier, and units aged more than 365 days cut by over 60%.
why_not_priced: Partly priced, and I am sizing it accordingly at +1.0. This is a direct counterparty speaking after Thor last guided [sizing note removed], and it is the single largest offset to the 'channel is still stuffed' read that the RVIA-minus-SSI gap generates - US retail registrations ran -19.0% in May and -20.7% in June against wholesale of -18.7% and -13.1%, which looks like inventory building until you find that the largest single buyer's lot is 17% lighter in units with almost no carryover model years. The reason it is not fully in the price is that it is eight weeks old, sits in a competitor's transcript rather than in any THO preview, and cuts against the direction every RV headline since has taken. If the market had folded it in, the pre-print commentary would be about a 2027 restock rather than about 'softer retail and shipment trends'. Marked snippet_only: I read the inventory figures from search output of the Q2 2026 call, not from a successful fetch of the transcript.

The sell-side Q4 bar is arithmetically above what the company's own guidance allows: nine-month revenue is GBP520.1m and full-year guidance is GBP655-665m, so the guided Q4 is GBP134.9-144.9m, while consensus Q4 is GBP148.17m and consensus FY is GBP665.16m — the top of the range to the penny. Manchester United can only meet consensus by exceeding a guide it raised on 27 May with five weeks of the fiscal year left.
why_not_priced: This is a two-analyst name and the consensus is a mechanical -9.76% year-on-year roll of last year's GBP164.1m Q4 rather than a residual off the company's own guide; if the market had done the subtraction, the previews would be framing a GBP135-145m quarter rather than quoting GBP148.17m as the number to beat, and the FY estimate would not sit at exactly the top of a range the company gave itself. The same arithmetic gap existed a year ago and resolved as a printed 'revenue miss'.

text: Two commercial deals were signed AFTER the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date and after the company last gave guidance on 27 May 2026, and both land only in the FY2027 outlook this release will introduce: a Betway training-kit partnership at a record ~GBP20m a year, which the club itself calls the biggest training-kit deal in world football (4 August 2026), and a SumUp shirt-sleeve deal the club calls its biggest ever sleeve partnership, against a prior DXC sleeve deal in the GBP10-20m a season range (8 September 2026).
why_not_priced: Both were sponsorship-trade and football-press stories, not financial-wire stories, and the equity market visibly did not reprice on them: the stock fell in 9 of the 10 sessions to 2026-09-10 and is -13.76% over 20 sessions, straight through the 8 September SumUp announcement, and is -15.5% from its 52-week high. If these were in the price, a name with a 38m-share float would not have made new short-term lows in the week its biggest-ever sleeve deal was signed. With two analysts covering and the last published model dated 27 May 2026 (Seeking Alpha's FY27 build, which lists only Champions League money, sporting bonuses and the Adidas clause), no sell-side FY2027 number can contain either deal. Combined they are roughly GBP20-30m of incremental, near-100%-margin annual commercial revenue against an adjusted EBITDA base of GBP200-210m.

text: 8.04% of a 38.19m-share free float is short with 9.25 days to cover — the highest days-to-cover in the day's universe — and the position was built by 10.8% in the last month, into a print at which the company is near-certain to introduce a record FY2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guide.
why_not_priced: The float is the unpriced part. Class A outstanding is 172.43m but the tradeable float is 38.19m after the Glazer Class B holding and the INEOS stake, so the quoted 10.54%-of-outstanding figure that screens and previews carry understates the real squeeze pressure by a factor of 2.6. Nothing in the baseline carries short interest at all, the option chain has 1,201 contracts of total open interest and a 66.7%-of-mid spread so it offers no hedge and no directional read, and the last four weeks of tape (-13.76%) are consistent with a short adding into a name nobody is defending. If the squeeze risk were priced, the chain would not be this empty and the borrow would show in a wider put skew rather than a null one.

text: The 10 June 2026 private placement of $550m of 5.36% senior secured notes due 2031, used to prepay the 3.79% notes due 2027, roughly doubles cash interest on the notes from about $16m to about $30m a year and adds $125m of net new principal — a real FY2027 drag on the net result that an adjusted-EBITDA guide will not show, plus write-off of unamortised issue costs on the prepaid notes in the reported quarter.
why_not_priced: It is priced as a headline and unpriced as arithmetic: the deal was covered as 'maturities extended', and the +$14m a year of cash interest does not appear in either of the two numbers the company guides on (revenue and adjusted EBITDA), so a record FY2027 EBITDA guide can print while the net-loss line and free cash flow stay where they are. If the market had done this arithmetic the previews would be discussing interest cover rather than only the Champions League revenue pool.

Glazer stake-sale specifics behind the 'sale speculation' in the 2026-09-17 TipRanks piece — no named buyer, no process, no date; rumour with no document, so worth 0.

Cracker Barrel pre-announced the quarter it is about to report: on 2026-07-20 it disclosed that first-eleven-week Q4 comps were restaurant -2.5% and retail +0.5% and that it now expects to 'achieve or exceed the high end' of FY26 revenue and 'exceed' its adjusted EBITDA outlook - while the Zacks consensus metric sheet dated 2026-09-18 still models Q4 restaurant comps at -3.4% and retail revenue -2.9%; for restaurant comps to reach -3.4% the final two weeks of the quarter would have had to run about -8%.
why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I size it accordingly. The July 20 8-K is public, so any serious holder has it; what is stale is the published consensus metric line, which two months later still carries a restaurant comp 0.9pp below the company's own disclosed eleven-week run rate and a negative retail number against a disclosed positive one. If the aggregated models had been refreshed to the disclosure, the Zacks comp estimate would read about -2.5% to -2.8% and the retail line would not be negative.

text: CBRL goes into this print with 25.26% of a 20.47m-share float sold short, 6.97 days to cover and the short book still growing (5.11m to 5.17m shares month on month), after a 20.8% twenty-session drawdown whose only identifiable cause is sector-wide - Placer.ai's August US dining traffic of -2.4% y/y knocked CBRL down ~11% on 2026-09-15 alongside CAKE, BLMN, EAT and PTLO - and that industry y/y statistic reads across to CBRL far more weakly than to peers because CBRL's own base quarter was boycott-collapsed: it reported Q1 FY2026 (Aug-Oct 2025) restaurant comps -4.7%, retail comps -8.5% and traffic -7%.
why_not_priced: If the market had priced the short-side asymmetry, the option book would be put-heavy and the skew wide; instead put/call open interest is 0.32 on 12,031 contracts and the 25-delta skew is +2.27 vol points against 51% realised vol - three times as much call as put open interest on a name a quarter of whose float is short. The option market is not paying for the downside the stock loan is positioned for, and the two cannot both be right.

text: The first FY2027 guide comes from a CEO six weeks into the job - David Deno started 2026-08-10, his inducement options struck at $56.10 against a $45.95 spot - and the company has been running a $9.99 Crispy Homestyle Chicken value platform plus a free-kids-toy offer from 2026-08-18 to 2026-10-18, i.e. straight through the first quarter he has to guide on; UBS's published band for the FY27 adjusted EBITDA guide is $160-200m against a $181m consensus.
why_not_priced: The new-CEO reset argument is in the wire and is priced; what is not is the specific resolution. Reading the two facts together - a CEO with no ownership of the FY27 plan and options 18% out of the money, and traffic currently being bought with a $9.99 entree through the guided quarter - the balance of the band sits in its lower half rather than above the $181m consensus. If the market had already settled on a lower-half guide, the consensus adjusted-EBITDA figure UBS is writing against would not still be $181m and the sell side would not have revised Q4 EPS estimates up 4.5% over the last 30 days while the stock fell 20%.

text: The $9.99 fall value platform runs to 2026-10-18 and the $6-8m of cash charges from exiting Maple Street Biscuit fall across Q4 FY2026 and FY2027, so their actual comp and margin contribution is only observable at the Q1 FY2027 print in December 2026, well after this exit window.

Chain-level Placer.ai or Black Box weekly traffic for CBRL in August-September 2026 - the only weekly figure findable ('traffic slid 5.3% the week of Aug. 25') traces to Restaurant Dive article 802176, which by article-ID sequence and content is the September 2025 boycott piece, not a 2026 datum; discarded on the date check

Any 8-K, 13D or company release between 2026-08-14 and 2026-09-22 - EDGAR shows nothing after the 2026-08-14 13G/A, so there is no company-specific cause for the 20.8% drawdown
A recoverable quarterly consensus for adjusted EPS - three sources give $0.10, $0.16 and $0.20, so no finding is sized off the EPS line
Insider open-market buying by Deno or any officer after the CEO transition - the only Form 4 activity is the grant of 3,565 RSUs and 7,434 options at $56.10 on 2026-08-10

Paychex's FY2027 guidance, set 2026-06-25, explicitly assumes 'no further changes to the Fed funds rate' and on that basis guides interest on funds held for clients DOWN to $195-205m from FY2026's $210.9m; the Fed then HIKED 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, with the dot plot at 4.00-4.25% for both year-end 2026 and 2027 and markets pricing a further hike.
why_not_priced: PAYX fell over the five sessions spanning the 16 September hike (sealed run_up_5d_pct -3.91%), so the market read a hiking Fed purely as a small-business demand negative and did not mark up a ~100%-margin float line that the company had guided down on an assumption the hike has now falsified. If this were priced, PAYX would have outperformed payroll peers after 16 September and the client-funds line would appear in the previews; the previews are entirely about hiring freezes. The dollars are deliberately sized small: per the 31 Aug 2025 10-Q the float is $4.98bn available-for-sale against only $775.2m of money-market and restricted cash equivalents, so ~86% of the portfolio reprices on the ladder rather than with Fed funds, making the direct FY27 benefit roughly $2-5m of a $195-205m line. What is worth more than the dollars is that a guided line gets revised the right way on a day the market is braced for the wrong way.

text: Paychex publishes its own free monthly Small Business Employment Watch, and it covers exactly the June-August quarter about to be reported: June 2026 printed a jobs index of 99.83, the highest since August 2025 and a fourth consecutive monthly improvement, and August printed 99.13, in line with the 2026 year-to-date average of 99.20, with weekly hours growth positive for a sixth straight month — so the 'flat employment levels' assumption underpinning the FY27 guide held through the reported quarter even as the stock lost 9.79% in 20 days on hiring-freeze fear.
why_not_priced: The drawdown has a named cause and it is a large-cap narrative, not this company's book: PAYX fell 3.9% in a single session on 2026-09-08 on fears that corporate hiring freezes would spread to small business. If the market were weighting Paychex's own client-base index over that narrative, the stock could not have fallen 3.9% in a session in the month after its own index printed a twelve-month high for the first month of the quarter being reported. The August release is at https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PAYX/stable-employment-levels-continue-for-u-s-small-businesses-in-k2eaefz17ugv.html (2026-09-01). Sized modestly because this is a free company press release on an 18-analyst, $41bn name — the opposite of the thin-coverage setup where an unpriced fact moves a stock hard.

text: The Q1 consensus revenue bar of $1.63bn is +5.8% year on year, sitting at the very top of the company's own 5-6% full-year guide, in the single quarter of FY27 carrying the hardest interest-on-funds comparison: Q1 FY26 interest was $47.6m and grew 27% on the Paycor balance step-up, struck with Fed funds at 4.25-4.50% against 3.50-3.75% through this quarter, and the Paycor balance benefit has now lapped.
why_not_priced: The street's Q1 number is published and the company's annual range is published, but the arithmetic between them — that consensus requires top-of-range growth in the quarter with the largest embedded rate headwind and no remaining acquisition inflation — is not in any preview I found, which all frame the quarter as a hiring-freeze question. If it were priced, the Q1 revenue estimate would sit nearer the middle of the guided range rather than at its ceiling.

text: Paychex's own September 2026 Small Business Employment Watch — the first read on whether the September hiring-freeze deterioration reached Paychex's client book, and the real test of the 'flat employment' guidance assumption — publishes around 2026-10-01, after the exit window closes.

The next FOMC meeting in late October 2026; markets price a further 25bp hike and the dot plot sits at 4.00-4.25%, which would break Paychex's 'no further changes to the Fed funds rate' assumption a second time and further lift the client-funds line above the $195-205m guide.

Insider buying: no open-market (code P) Form 4 purchases in September 2026 — the only September filing found was a 334-share gift disposition by B. Thomas Golisano on 2026-09-01. No insider conviction signal into a 13% drawdown from the high.

Capital return catalyst at this print: Paychex raises its dividend in April/May (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and most recently to $1.19 from $1.08), not in September, and the $1bn buyback authorization dates from 2026-01-16 with ~$389m still unspent. Nothing new is due on 09-23.

Paycor integration distress: searched for attrition, layoffs and restructuring and found the opposite — ~$100m of expense synergies largely complete, revenue synergies tracking to the high end of the 30-50bp target, and employee attrition better than Paycor's own history.
Executive change: no CFO or senior leadership 8-K in September 2026; Bob Schrader remains CFO.

Peer read-through for a negative: Paycom raised FY26 guidance in early August and Paylocity guided FY27 revenue to ~7% growth on 2026-08-04. No HCM peer has flagged a small-business volume break since Paychex last spoke.

PEO/insurance loss-ratio blowout: looked for evidence that medical and workers-comp inflation is compressing the PEO take rate; found only generic medical-inflation commentary and management calling medical inflation a PEO tailwind. No company-level number to size.

The FY2026 10-K's quantitative Item 7A rate-sensitivity table, which would have let finding 1 be sized in dollars rather than bounded — the document is too large to retrieve that section through the available fetchers.

General Mills' fiscal Q1 2027 ended 2026-08-30, and on 2026-09-08 — nine days after the quarter closed — the company reaffirmed the full FY2027 guide AND disclosed quarter-specific consumption data (Q1 retail dollar sales +2 points versus Q4, 8 of its top 10 categories gaining dollar share, cereal category dollar sales +2 points, taste-forward cereal brands +5 points, base pound volume from -10% at end-FY2025 to +2% at end-FY2026); so the guidance line this stock actually trades on has already been marked to a completed quarter, and a guidance cut on 2026-09-23 would be a reversal 15 days after a post-close reaffirmation.
why_not_priced: Partially priced and I say so. What is not in the price is the TIMING: the wire copy read 'reaffirms guidance at a conference', which the market treats as a mid-quarter statement, and the quarter had in fact already closed. If the market had read it as a post-close pre-announcement, the stock would not have de-rated a further 8% into the print and the front-expiry straddle would not be 1.8x this name's median realised reaction. The specific observable: an implied event move of 5.55% on a name whose guidance range was marked to the completed quarter a fortnight ago.

text: At the same 2026-09-08 fireside chat management said input-cost inflation is tracking toward the HIGH END of the guided 4-5% range with hedge coverage only 6-9 months out (~9 months on crops), while on the 2026-07-01 call it had already said fiscal 2027 profit is weighted to the second half because 'the impact of inflation net of cost savings is expected to be negative in the first quarter' — so the quarter being reported is the one where cost leverage is worst and the $750m of FY2027 savings has not yet phased in.
why_not_priced: The 2026-09-08 press release headline was 'reaffirms annual guidance'; the high-end-of-range inflation detail and the 6-9 month hedge window sat in the fireside chat and not in the release, so it travelled through transcript coverage rather than the wire. If it were fully in the price, the 30-day consensus drift would not have gone UP 1.4% (from $0.71 to $0.72) over exactly the window containing that statement. That said, it is inside a guided range, which is why it is sized below one point.

text: The option market is paying an event-implied 5.55% (7.75% front-expiry straddle, 38.3% ATM IV) with a +2.75 put skew on a name whose last seven prints have a median absolute reaction of 3.06% and a maximum of 8.53%, while the short base — 46.0m shares, 8.64% of float, 5.60 days to cover — is already covering from 49.1m, and the entire +8.53% reaction to the 2026-07-01 print has been given back (spot $35.805 against a $40.08 director-grant price on 2026-08-30).
why_not_priced: I am signing against the skew, so I have to say why the option market is wrong about THIS print: the downside being bought is dividend-cut and structural-derating contagion — Campbell's cut its dividend 36% on 2026-09-03 and GIS fell 3.25% the same day, and GIS now yields ~6.8% — but a dividend cut is not an event this print can deliver. GIS declared its $0.61 quarterly dividend with the 2026-07-01 release (paid 2026-08-03) and the next board declaration sits with the late-September annual-meeting cycle, ex-date 2026-10-12, outside the window. If the skew were about the quarter rather than about the payout and the sector, the put/call open-interest ratio would not be 0.55. The counterweight is real and is why this is [sizing note removed].7 rather than 2: the resolved record has a hunter losing 11 points to a large put skew, and a covering short base is a reason to shrink a negative, not a licence to enlarge a positive.

text: General Mills is a PLAINTIFF, with Mars, Kellanova and McKee Foods, in an antitrust suit filed 2026-09-04 in federal court in Chicago alleging US sugar producers fixed granulated sugar prices from January 2017 to at least October 2024 — a gain contingency, not a liability, that no preview treats as an asset and that cannot resolve on 2026-09-23.

The Brazil business (Yoki, Kitano) was sold to 3coracoes for a R$800m base price and CLOSED on 2026-09-03, which is fiscal Q2 2027 and not the quarter being reported; the $1,032m non-cash pre-tax held-for-sale valuation loss was already taken in Q4 FY2026, so any final close adjustment and CTA recycling lands in the December print.

The next quarterly dividend declaration falls with the late-September board/annual-meeting cycle, ex-date 2026-10-12, payable 2026-11-03 — so the payout question the 6.8% yield is pricing is not settled by this print.

A Pet/Blue Buffalo negative worth filing: GIS's own 2026-09-08 line that Blue Buffalo Wilderness 'may take 18 months to 2 years to return to growth' plus the guided low-single-digit FY27 retail-inventory headwind is pre-guided, Pet is only ~14% of sales ($610m of $4.52bn in the year-ago quarter) against a North America Retail segment management says gained share in 8 of its top 10 categories, and the independent read cuts the other way — Chewy on 2026-09-09 said the pet market 'did not meaningfully recover... but also did not deteriorate further' and RAISED its FY outlook (https://investor.chewy.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Chewy-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). Net of the rest of the company this is not a finding, so it is not one.

A 'low bar on seasonality' argument: $0.72 is 23.2% of the $3.10 FY27 midpoint against $0.86 / ~$3.60 = 23.9% for the prior year. The bar is normal for a GIS Q1, not conspicuously low, so I dropped this line rather than sizing it.

Insider signal: all Form 4s since 2026-06-01 are routine — non-employee director retainer shares issued 2026-05-31 at $33.65 and 2026-08-30 at $40.08 under the 2022 Stock Compensation Plan (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040704/000162828026059544/wk-form4_1788200689.xml). No open-market cluster.
Quiet 8-K: EDGAR shows NO 8-K filed by CIK 0000040704 since the 2026-07-01 results 8-K; the 2026-09-08 reaffirmation was a press release only. Nothing hidden in the filing record.
Bernstein's Underperform on GIS/CPB/CAG/KHC turned out to be dated JUNE 2026, not September, despite September-looking search framing — checked and discarded as a driver of the current drawdown.

A causal, company-specific explanation for the -12.5% 20-day run-up beyond sector de-rating, the Campbell's dividend cut on 09-03, a JPMorgan Sell reiteration and an Evercore target trim to $38 on 09-14: there isn't one, and an unexplained drawdown on a 17-analyst mega-cap is not evidence of over-reaction.

Free September Circana/Nielsen takeaway data for cereal or pet that post-dates the company's own 2026-09-08 disclosure — Circana's pet release would not render and nothing else is public at that granularity.
A quantified Q1 FY2027 figure in any primary document not already carried by the wire. There is none; this is a mega-cap with full coverage, which is the reason every size here is small.

KB Home goes into this print with average community count up roughly 8% YoY (Q3-2025 average 259 / ending 264; Q2-2026 average 278 up 9%, Q3-2026 ending guided 270-280) and a cancellation rate of 12% of gross orders against 17% in the year-ago Q3 - so its net-order line has two mechanical tailwinds that Lennar, whose -9% order print is what the market marked KBH down on, does not have.
why_not_priced: KBH fell 12.6% over 20 sessions and roughly tracked Lennar's post-print de-rating. If the market had done this arithmetic it would not have applied Lennar's -9% pace decline one-for-one to a company carrying ~8% more selling communities and 5 percentage points fewer cancellations: at Q3-2025's 3.8 monthly absorption per community KBH needs only 3.4 (a -11% pace decline, worse than Lennar's) on 280 communities to print net orders down just 3% YoY. Every published preview frames tonight as 'will orders hold' in the abstract and none of them carries the community base. Net of the rest of the company: deliveries and margin are both inside the company's own June guide and therefore cannot surprise much either way, so this line is not being offset by a hidden negative elsewhere in the release - the offset is the forward guide, which I size separately and negatively below.

text: The Q3 delivery guide of 2,600-2,800 homes implies only 57-62% conversion of the 4,526-home backlog KBH carried into the quarter, against 66.5% actually converted in Q2-2026 (2,395 delivered from an opening backlog of 3,604) and ~71% in Q3-2025 (3,393 from ~4,764) - so the revenue guide carries a conversion cushion.
why_not_priced: It is arithmetic off two primary documents that no aggregator publishes - the opening backlog is derived (4,526 ending + 2,395 delivered - 3,317 net orders = 3,604 opening), and the conversion series is not in any preview. But I size it small and say why: this outcome lands INSIDE what the company guided on 23 June, so the market has already been told to expect it, and the conversion rate legitimately falls as the built-to-order mix lengthens cycle times. The honest read is that it lowers the probability of a delivery MISS rather than creating a beat, and the +0.5 reflects exactly that and nothing more.

text: Two peer builders printed sequential gross-margin IMPROVEMENT in windows that overlap KBH's June-August quarter and that both landed after KBH last spoke on 23 June: Lennar's Q3 (identical 31 August quarter end) went 15.3% to 15.8% with incentives moderating to 12%, and Hovnanian's quarter ended 31 July was its SECOND consecutive sequential gross-margin improvement - which is the same shape as KBH's guided step from 15.2% to 16.0-16.6%.
why_not_priced: The wire framing of Lennar was 'double miss, guidance cut, 52-week low' and of the margin line specifically 'down from 17.5% a year ago'. The SEQUENTIAL direction - up 50bp with incentives falling - is the reading that bears on KBH's guided step and it is not what the headlines carried, and Hovnanian's 20 August print is barely covered at all. Sized small deliberately: KBH's 16.0-16.6% is a guided number, so confirming it only removes downside rather than creating upside, and the step KBH needs (80-140bp) is larger than the 50bp Lennar achieved. If the market had fully priced a confirmed margin step, KBH would not have de-rated in lockstep with LEN over the last 20 sessions.

text: KBH's standing FY2026 guide ($4.90-5.30bn housing revenue, 16.1-16.5% housing gross margin, 10,500-11,000 deliveries) arithmetically back-loads a Q4 that needs roughly $1.45-1.85bn of housing revenue - flat to -13% YoY after quarters down 23%, 27% and ~20% - at an IMPLIED Q4 housing gross margin of about 17-18%, while Lennar has just guided its own Q4 (same calendar quarter) to a FLAT 15.5-16.0% and said the incentive cost of rate buydowns is the emerging pressure.
why_not_priced: The FY range itself is wire copy; the implied Q4 decomposition is not, and no preview I could find states it. Derived from primary documents only: Q1 housing revenue 2,370 x $452,100 = $1.071bn at 15.3%, Q2 2,395 x $461,900 = $1.106bn at 15.2%, Q3 guided $1.275bn midpoint at 16.3% - which leaves roughly $291m of gross profit on ~$1.65bn of Q4 revenue, i.e. ~17.6%. If the market had priced a guide cut, KBH would not be trading 8.0% ABOVE its 52-week low while Lennar made a NEW 52-week low on its own print six days ago; that gap is the part of this that is unmarked. Shrunk from a standalone -3.0 to -2.4 per the crowded-short rule: 12.91% of float and 8.89 days to cover is a squeeze mechanism in its own right, and this exact setup produced +16.65% on a worse EPS number in June.

text: KB Home will deliver this print and set its FY guide with no permanent CFO: Robert Dillard resigned effective 8 May 2026 with no successor disclosed in the 8-K, and none has been announced in the four and a half months since - under a CEO, Robert McGibney, who only took the seat on 1 March 2026 and is in his second full quarter.
why_not_priced: The resignation itself was an April news item and is stale; what is not priced is the DURATION - a $3.0bn builder giving its most important guide of the year in its fourth month without a permanent CFO. A new CEO plus an interim finance chief is the standard setup for resetting an outlook rather than defending it, and it lowers the odds of a bold capital-return announcement that would otherwise be the obvious offset at 0.77x book with $775m of authorisation live. If this were priced there would be a preview naming it; none of the four previews I read mentions the CFO seat. I size it small and label the inference as inference: the 8-K is a document, the behavioural conclusion from it is not.

text: The Census/HUD August 2026 New Residential Sales release is scheduled for 24 September 2026 - two days after this print and one day after the exit - and July already printed 607,000 SAAR, down 10.5% month-on-month, with 488,000 new homes for sale. The FTC second request of 2026-06-11 is not close to resolved: Cintas is due to complete its compliance response between September and November 2026, the FTC has issued expansive civil investigative demands to third-party industry participants, and market-implied approval odds have fallen from ~85% on 25 Aug to ~70%, with Bernstein now expecting an early-2027 close against management's stated 'second half of calendar 2026'. Management will almost certainly have to address the timing on the 10:00 ET call, but the regulatory event itself cannot land by the 2026-09-23 close.

The 8-K of 2026-06-12 confirms the Second Request extends the HSR waiting period until 30 days after both parties substantially comply — a clock that by construction runs past the exit window, and whose outcome (clearance, divestiture, or a $350m reverse termination fee to UniFirst if blocked on antitrust grounds) is the single largest unpriced binary on this equity.

Extra FY2027 workday: I counted it independently (Q1 FY2027 = 65 workdays vs 64 in Q1 FY2026 after the observed 3 July holiday, a +1.56pp revenue tailwind concentrated in this quarter against the +0.40pp full-year figure). Management stated exactly this on the 2026-07-15 call — 'The first quarter of fiscal year 27 has 1 extra day... The second quarter has the same number of workdays. The third quarter has 1 less workday. And then the fourth quarter has 1 more workday' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/22/cintas-ctas-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). A number management reads out on a transcript is not unpriced.

Fuel cost as a gross-margin surprise — the one lead I thought I had, and it falsified. Diesel looked dramatic (EIA monthly: Jun-Aug 2026 avg $5.147 vs $3.707 a year earlier, +38.8%, and DOWN from $5.341 in Mar-May 2026), which would have implied an easing YoY comp on the record 51.0% gross margin. But Cintas runs a gasoline van fleet, and on the correct series the comp barely moves: gasoline Jun-Aug 2026 $4.013 vs $3.136, +27.9%, against Mar-May 2026 $4.073 vs $3.139, +29.8% (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=emm_epmr_pte_nus_dpg&f=m). Applying management's own stated elasticity — fuel is ~100bp of revenue and a 20% fuel price move is ~20bp of margin — the YoY fuel headwind eases by roughly 2bp quarter-on-quarter, i.e. nothing. Dropped rather than filed.

Cintas M&A in the quarter: no bolt-on acquisition 8-K or press release between 2026-07-15 and today, so no inorganic revenue the street has not modelled. The only EDGAR events since the print are a 2026-08-03 8-K promoting Jim Rozakis to President & COO, a 2026-08-27 8-K on a director not standing for re-election, the 2026-09-15 DEF 14A/ARS, and Form 4 clusters on 2026-08-12 and 2026-09-17 — all routine for a company whose executives sell continuously under plan.

Competitor read-through: Vestis (the nearest pure-play) reported its quarter ended 2026-07-03 on 2026-08-11 with revenue -1.8% and pounds processed -4.5%, and left its FY2026 revenue growth outlook unchanged at (2.0)% to flat (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001967649/000162828026055485/vstsq3fy26earningsrelease-.htm). Discarded: Vestis has been losing share to Cintas for two years, so its volume decline is as likely to be a Cintas tailwind as an industry signal, and it is exactly the narrow-proxy trap — it also overlaps only one of Cintas's three months.
UniFirst as a direct counterparty on the same calendar quarter: UNF's fiscal Q4 ends late August and is reported in October, so nothing from the acquiree covers Jun-Aug 2026 ahead of this print.

Cintas hiring as a wearer-growth proxy: careers.cintas.com currently shows 244 route service and 119 service sales openings, but no archived time series exists to compare against, so the level carries no information.

Employment-sensitivity as a transmission channel: no company or direct-counterparty statement connects Jun-Aug small-business payrolls to Cintas wearer counts for this quarter, and Cintas's organic growth has accelerated (7.8% in Q1 FY26 to 8.4% in Q4 FY26) through a soft employment backdrop on price and cross-sell. Left as a hypothesis, not a finding.

Financing: no debt issuance, 424B, FWP or shelf takedown since the deal was signed. The $2.8bn cash leg is covered by committed bridge financing from Morgan Stanley, KeyBank and Wells Fargo arranged in March, and the FY2027 guide's ~$105m interest expense assumption explicitly excludes UniFirst, so there is no pre-funding event to sign either way.
Proxy/governance: PRE 14A 2026-08-28 and DEF 14A 2026-09-15 carry nothing unusual — no share authorisation increase is needed for the ~14m shares of stock consideration against 400.7m outstanding.

The +8.74% five-session run-up rests on a 15 Sep 8-K that renames Building Products to 'Building Performance Solutions' and Consumer Products to 'Trade & Specialty Solutions' and states in terms that the change is name-only — 'The changes are to the segment names only and do not affect the composition of the segments or the historical financial results' — yet the stock re-rated ~10% in a day on the data-centre reading of the new name, when the underlying data-centre business was already disclosed on the 24 June call at ~$13m for all of FY2026 and 'at least that much' in Q1 FY2027, i.e. roughly 4% of a $331m quarter.
why_not_priced: The price moved, but on a narrative rather than on arithmetic. If the market had priced the arithmetic, a filing that explicitly disclaims any effect on segment composition or historical results would not have added ~10% of market capitalisation in one session, and the stock would not now sit 5.4% off its 52-week high having risen 8.74% in five days into a print it has sold four times running. The number the pop is about ($13m a quarter, guided in June) has been public for three months and is small enough that tonight's segment tables cannot corroborate a re-rating of that size — they can only fail to.

text: Midwest hot-rolled coil hit a four-year high of $1,202.40/short ton on 20 August 2026, roughly $1,200 through late August against about $800 a year earlier (+50% YoY) — squarely across Worthington's June–August fiscal Q1, on a company that converts purchased steel and whose last print was an EPS miss ($0.97 vs $1.06) on a 17% sales gain, i.e. a pure margin failure at lower steel prices than these.
why_not_priced: It is partly priced and I have sized it accordingly rather than claiming otherwise — HRC is a public series and the five-estimate consensus has been cut 5.1% in 90 days, which is what analysts marking it down looks like. What is not in the cut is the second-order transmission through the unconsolidated JVs, where Worthington books equity income it does not control: ClarkDietrich's contribution already collapsed to $21.9m in FY2026 from $40.8m in FY2025 and to $6.1m from $12.9m in Q4 alone, and management's answer on the June call was that it is 'pretty confident that's a trough' — a hope, not a number. If this were fully priced the $0.75 consensus would not still imply flat adjusted EPS against a year-ago $0.74 on revenue up 9%.

text: WAVE, the 50/50 Armstrong JV that supplied $118.1m of Worthington's equity income in FY2026 against $295.8m of total adjusted EBITDA — about 40% of company earnings — is disclosed by the OTHER partner as improving: Armstrong reported WAVE equity earnings of $2m in calendar Q2 2026 against $1m a year earlier and guided to a step-up in the second half.
why_not_priced: Five analysts cover Worthington and Armstrong is a different sector with a different analyst set, so the read-through is made by almost nobody; a third party disclosed the direction of ~40% of Worthington's earnings eight weeks before Worthington did. If it were priced, the 90-day estimate trend would not be down 5.1% into a quarter whose largest single earnings contributor a counterparty has said is rising.

text: Worthington signed a Fifth Amended and Restated $500m unsecured revolver on 2026-08-31 with a $300m accordion, pushing maturity from 2028 to 2031 at a 12.5bp facility fee, and drew nothing on it — a filing three weeks old that no wire covered.
why_not_priced: It is not priced because nobody wrote about it, and it is worth almost nothing, which is the honest answer rather than a reason to size it up. I asked the question the money answers and got the benign one: undrawn at signing, a 12.5bp facility fee and a three-year maturity extension are what a syndicate underwrites for a company with no leverage problem, and the stated use is 'working capital and other general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures and acquisitions'. It corroborates the M&A capacity management named as a priority after spending $300m on Elgen and LSI in FY2026 on $170m of free cash flow. It is filed so that the financing line on this name reads as 'checked, benign' and cannot later be mistaken for distress.

The company's own quarterly path puts Q4 FY26 revenue at roughly $11.5-12.5m against the $12.28m the only sourceable consensus implies, because Q4 is the first FULL quarter of the Adzenys authorized-generic mix shift that cut Q3 ADHD revenue to $9.1m from $13.2m in each of Q1 and Q2, layered on the seasonal June-quarter ADHD trough (FY25 went $15.4m in Q3 to $13.1m in Q4).
why_not_priced: Three analysts carry an FY26 number and nobody has published a Q4 split; if the $12.28m implied quarter were being actively modelled the stock would not have added 15.08% in five sessions on 26k shares a day with the company silent since the 16 September date announcement. What would be visibly different if it were priced: a published Q4 revenue estimate somewhere, and a flat-to-down tape into the print rather than a five-day squeeze.

text: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA swings to roughly minus $7.5m from plus $9.2m in FY2025 — a ~$17m reversal on a $24.6m market cap — and Q4 is the worst quarter of the year by design, because management guided on the Q3 call that Q4 sales and marketing would rise $1-2m and G&A $0.2-0.3m sequentially off an already negative $2.8m Q3.
why_not_priced: The four quarterly adjusted-EBITDA figures (-0.6, -0.8, -2.8 and a guided-worse Q4) have never been added up in one place, and a full-year release is precisely where they get added up on the first line of the table. If this were priced there would be a published FY26 EBITDA estimate to check it against, and the stock would not have rallied into it.

text: Cash falls to roughly $21-23m at 30 June 2026 from $26.7m at 31 March and $31.0m at the start of the year, against $10.4m drawn on an Eclipse Business Capital revolver whose $14.5m borrowing base is receivables-driven and therefore shrinking with the ADHD revenue that generates it.
why_not_priced: A full-year release plus the 10-K is where a liquidity paragraph or a concurrent capital raise would surface, and with 10.73m shares outstanding a raise is unusually dilutive per share; if the market were pricing that, the pre-print tape would not be +15% in five days. What would look different if priced: put demand, which cannot exist here because there is no chain, or a discount to the $26.7m cash balance rather than an enterprise value of $20.8m.

text: The 30 June fiscal year end is the annual intangible impairment testing date, AYTU carries $42.49m of intangibles that are overwhelmingly ADHD and pediatric product rights, the ADHD line is running 41% below prior year and is being deliberately deemphasised, and the Metadate CD licence from Lannett was terminated by mutual agreement on 23 June 2026 — seven days before the fiscal year closed.
why_not_priced: The Metadate termination 8-K was filed on 25 June into a name with 26k shares a day of volume and no coverage; it frames its own materiality downward ('Net revenue of Metadate CD reported by the Company for the Quarter Ended March 31, 2026 was $49,000') while saying the full Termination Agreement will only be filed with the annual report, so the carrying-value consequence is deferred to exactly tonight's document. If the market had priced an impairment, stockholders' equity of $35.1m would not be supporting a $24.6m market cap the way it currently appears to.

If the market held current script data, a stock with three estimates and a $24.6m cap would show it in coverage or in volume rather than 26k shares a day.

text: The stock has added 15.08% in five sessions on 26,037 shares a day of average volume with no company news of any kind since the 16 September earnings-date announcement, and the 20-day run-up is -0.87% — so the entire move is a five-day pre-print bid into a 7.56m float, with short interest at 4.43% far too small to be its cause or to squeeze against a disappointment.
why_not_priced: This is a fact about who owns the stock going in rather than about the company, and it is the fact the baseline most conspicuously cannot carry: with no option chain there is no skew and therefore no market statement about the risk, and the sealed baseline's expected_move_pct of 1.46% is a median of a distribution running -17.93% to +91.85%, which under-describes the event by an order of magnitude. If this run-up were informed rather than anticipatory, there would be a news item behind it and there is none.

The short base is moderately crowded (11.9% of float, 9.4 days to cover) and grew 8.2% into the 2026-08-31 settlement. The stock went into the print at a fresh 52-week low ($2.80, -6.2% on the day, -13% over the month against -9% for the apparel group), and option open interest is 5:1 calls. why_not_priced: Partly priced. A 21.6% implied move against a 10.5% median says the options market expects a large move but gives no direction, since skew is null. If shorts had already covered, short interest would have fallen into the print rather than risen 8.2%, and the stock would not be making lows on print day. What is not in the price is only the asymmetry, not a fact about the quarter.

The company's own dates for the Georgia (Pendergrass) factory have slipped about a quarter. On June 22 it said site acceptance testing would be done by end of August 2026 and the production ramp would start in Q3 CY2026 (May 14 said the same Q3 ramp). On Sept 17, testing was still 'underway' and the ramp 'remains on track for the fourth quarter of calendar 2026'. The only FY27 (Jul 2026-Jun 2027) revenue consensus found is still $102.29M, against a factory that has not yet shipped and a $53M binding reservation that covers all of calendar 2027.
why_not_priced: The company framed the new date as 'remains on track' and the wire headlines repeated it ('production ramp on track for Q4 2026'), so no piece of wire copy reports a slip; you see it only by putting the June 22 and Sept 17 releases side by side. If the slip were priced, the FY27 revenue consensus would have come down from $102M; stockanalysis still shows $102.29M from 5 analysts, and the most recent note (Needham, Sept 15) came before the Sept 17 release. The call is the first place analysts can ask for a first-shipment date and FY27 revenue. Against that, the stock has already faded since Sept 17, so some of this may be priced, which is why the size is small.

The FY2026 target of '>100% retail volume growth' cannot be reached with the network the company has. It was reaffirmed on 2026-06-16. FY2025 retail volume was 51,110 (Q1 7,545 + Q2 10,385 + Q3 14,020 + Q4 19,160), so the target needs >102,220 units. H1 comes to about 35,000 (Q1 16,530 plus a Q2 guide of 18-19k), which leaves ~67,000 for H2, or ~33.5k a quarter, against a Q2 run-rate of ~18.5k. The company's own press-release stream up to 2026-09-16 shows no superstore opened after Tianjin on 2026-03-31. Chongqing (2026-05-21), Shijiazhuang (JV, 2026-06-02) and Shaoxing (2026-07-20) are announced projects only. So the Q3 guide given on 09-24, with Q3 almost over, should land around +45-65% year on year, and the FY target has to be cut or dropped.
why_not_priced: The Q2 guide had made the arithmetic possible since June, and the stock has fallen ~29% since (weekly close ~$1.51 after the Q1 print, $1.075 now). Some of this is probably priced, and that is why the size is below the name's 8.5% median earnings move. It is not fully priced because no sell-side number exists to reset. The company has not withdrawn the target, and the reaffirmation in the 06-23 FAQ and at the 06-25 investor day is still the last word. With no analyst to downgrade, the formal cut and the Q3 run-rate are only seen when the release prints. If the market had already priced the cut, a Q3 guide would not matter and the stock would not have sold -10.4% on the last deceleration.

text: Of the December 2025 US$50M share subscription at US$2.859 per ADS, Prestige Shine Group's US$30M still appears unfunded. The 2026-06-29 6-K closed only a US$15M NIO-designated tranche, and no closing 6-K has been filed since. The subscription price is now 2.66x the $1.075 spot. Cash was only RMB47.4M at 2026-03-31 against RMB745M of current liabilities. The money was earmarked for the four to six 2026 superstores, and none has opened. If the release updates that commitment, the likely forms are repricing, termination or a slip. Closing at $2.859 would be the positive surprise, and nothing observable points to it.
why_not_priced: Mostly priced, which is why the size is small. A stock at 38% of the subscription price implies the market already assumes Prestige Shine will not fund at $2.859. The release is simply the first place a status update can appear, and there has been no 6-K since 2026-07-01. Financing question asked and answered: the money buys superstores, and none has opened (see the first finding), so there is no ramp to corroborate. A going-concern paragraph was carried in the prior 20-F. That leans negative, but the sign of the in-window resolution is genuinely unknown, so the range spans zero.

CarMax's own ABS servicer reports through August 2026 show no new credit deterioration in the securitised Tier 1 book, which the 10-Q puts at 95.6% of the portfolio. The 2025-3 trust at 13 months (31+ day delinquency 1.75%, cumulative net loss 0.49%) tracks 2024-3 at the same age a year earlier (1.63%, 0.60%). The problem 2023 vintage (trust 2023-4) deteriorated April to August 2026 by +1.22pp of delinquency, against +1.11pp over the same months of 2025, and its cumulative net loss accrual slowed. So a repeat of Q2 FY26's $71.3m reserve build for the 2022-2023 vintages looks unlikely.
why_not_priced: Previews cite only the May allowance ratio (2.95%, up from 2.78%) and the Manheim index as the credit tells (traderc 2026-09-19). None cites the June-August trust data. If the market had read these reports, put skew would not still be rising into the print on a name whose last big credit shock was a vintage build. ORTEX has put/call 2.4 standard deviations above its average. The caveat, which the size reflects: consensus EPS up 11.5% YoY already assumes no repeat build, so this removes a tail rather than moving the bar. The Tier 2 book, whose day-one provisions are the live worry, is not in these trusts.

text: The revenue bar of $6.94bn (+5.3% YoY) implies roughly flat retail units against a Q2 FY26 comparison of -6.3% comps. Management blamed that quarter on demand pulled into Q1 by tariffs and on price competitiveness hurt by depreciation. Q1 FY27 ran a two-year comp stack of +7.3% (+8.1% then -0.8%). Cox says used retail sales strengthened through August, with retail days' supply falling from 46 to 44, so units and revenue probably clear the bar by about 3%.
why_not_priced: Consensus revenue has been too low two prints running. Q1 needed an 8% beat, and the Q2 bar still implies little unit recovery against the easiest comparison in years. If the comparison were priced, published revenue estimates would sit nearer $7.2bn than $6.94bn. The counterweight is already in the size: this is arithmetic anyone can do from public numbers, the buy-side whisper is probably above $6.94bn, and the June print showed this holder base selling a revenue beat. I sized the reaction at 0.4, not the ~1.0 the fact alone might carry.

It is an industry proxy, and whether it reaches this company is a hypothesis this quarter, so the size is small.

Q3 (Jun-Aug) Brent averaged ~$87 (June $85, July $84, August $91 per EIA) against a June guide struck at spot fuel that management said moved EPS by less than $0.01 versus the March guide, which had assumed Brent $85 for Q3 — so the Q3 fuel headwind the previews cite is small, and Carnival's habitual beat of its own guide (Q2 beat March guidance by $100m) should carry Q3 EPS to roughly $1.38-1.42 against a $1.35 bar held at the guide.
why_not_priced: The wire frames fuel as 'Brent +34% since the Q2 report' (BofA, 2026-09-27), measured from the late-June trough (~$74) rather than from the fuel basis embedded in the Q3 guide; if the market had priced a Q3 beat, consensus would sit above the $1.35 guide rather than on it, as it usually does for a company that beats every quarter. Small size because a guide beat is exactly what this name's holders have sold twice this year, and because bunker prices do not map one-for-one onto Brent (Q2 fuel was $793/mt in a >$100 Brent quarter).

text: The Q4/FY guide will be struck at spot fuel with Brent at ~$106 on 2026-09-28 against a June basis equivalent to ~$80 Brent for Q4 (March assumption, unchanged in June to within $0.01), a ~30%+ rise that on the company's own sensitivity (~$46m of Q4 net income per 10%, derived from $102m remainder-of-year less $56m Q3) is ~$0.10-0.13 of Q4 EPS — deeper than the $0.07 Q4 cut BofA made (to $0.20), so the Q4 guide risks printing below the Street's Q4 number.
why_not_priced: Only partially: every preview says fuel, and the stock is -15% in a month and at a 16-month low on it. The residual is mechanical — Carnival guides at spot, not the backwardated curve (EIA 2H26 ~$90), and spot is at a local high on the eve of the print; BofA's $0.07 Q4 cut is roughly a 15% fuel move on the sensitivity, not 30%. If the market had priced a spot-fuel guide, Q4 estimates would sit nearer $0.13-0.15 than $0.20 and the option market would not be paying up for calls.

Akamai's 8-K of 2026-09-24 says it issued Jabil a build request under their existing server-manufacturing MSA and authorised Jabil to buy about $1.7bn of memory components on consignment, which Jabil buys back at cost as it uses them. The request is tied to Akamai's $11.6bn, seven-year Anthropic cloud deal, arrived after Jabil last spoke on 2026-06-17, and is for a customer and program Jabil has never quantified. With DRAM now over half of a server's bill of materials, the full build is plausibly a multi-billion-dollar FY27-28 revenue program that Jabil can fold into the FY27 guide on 2026-09-30.
why_not_priced: It is partly priced: JBL rose 4.8% in the afternoon session after the 8-K (https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/stockstory-2026-9-25-why-jabil-jbl-stock-is-trading-up-today). That is roughly $1.5bn of market cap, and it is also roughly what a ~$3bn program at a ~5% core margin is worth. What is not priced is the size of the program. Jabil has not said how much revenue it brings or when, and four sessions is too short for eleven analysts to rebuild FY27 models that sit at $15.60 core EPS. If the market had priced a larger program, the stock would have recovered more of the $429-to-$300 drawdown and the skew would be more call-bid than -1.1. The offset is that pass-through memory at cost adds revenue but little margin, so it can pull the FY27 margin guide below the >6% management framed in June, which the market could read as dilution.

text: Domo's own 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, filed 2026-09-03 with no press release and no call, shows the business Progress bought is shrinking faster than the $318M trailing revenue in the July deal deck implies. Subscription RPO is $387.6M against $409.8M a year earlier (-5.4%) and $412.9M one quarter earlier (-6% sequentially), current RPO is $214.4M against $220.2M (-2.6%), and revenue is $76.8M (-3.7%). The first Domo-inclusive guide and ARR bridge tonight are therefore likely to dilute the organic ARR growth management calls 'the clearest read' (+2%) towards flat.
why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. The deterioration is already known in outline: Domo's merger proxy said Progress cut its bid from $432M to $400M over 'greater-than-expected deterioration in Domo's revenue and ARR' (https://www.utahmoneywatch.com/domo-chapter-2-behind-its-400-million-asset-sale-domo-was-preparing-for-a-possible-chapter-11-bankruptcy-filing/, 2026-08-20), there was a Seeking Alpha downgrade, and the stock has fallen from ~$46 to $40 since early September. The RPO numbers sit in a target-company 10-Q that PRGS previews do not cite. If they were priced, previews would be framing Domo's contribution as declining revenue rather than as '$318M revenue, 2,400 customers'. Netted against the rest of the company: Progress standalone (~75% of pro forma revenue) pre-announced a strong quarter. Domo's FY26 revenue add is mechanically positive, roughly $55-60M over the ~70 days after close. At a 6% non-GAAP margin, before any cuts, Domo is roughly break-even for Q4 EPS after revolver interest, so the headline FY revenue guide goes up and the EPS guide is unlikely to fall. That offset is why this is sized small. It is shrunk further for the 11.9%-of-float short.

**The disclosed track:** 14.5% (Q4 FY25) → 14.1% (Q1 FY26) → **12.9% (Q2 FY26)** [11][15]. Miller in June: "The gap between our current incentive levels of 12.9% and normalized levels of 4% to 6% is narrowing for the first time in three years... Demand is real, deferred, and building" [11]. He described the Q2 decline as "the first real and potentially sustainable decline" after several years of rising incentives [15].

**What the market expects, and how I know.** The market expects the ~16% gross-margin guide to be met, because that is what the sell-side models embed [14] and it is what management guided [11]. But the market plainly does *not* believe in the durability of the trend, and I can evidence that: the stock is down ~16% since the Q2 print that delivered the good incentive number [26], it trades below stated book [26], and BofA cut to $70 on 0.9x forward tangible book specifically on "continued pressure on return on tangible equity," with FY27/FY28 EPS estimates 6% and 11% below consensus [10][25].

**Why the quarter is genuinely at risk.** HousingWire's framing, which I think is the sharpest single line written about this print: "every 10-basis-point move in mortgage rates has essentially the same impact on affordability as a 1% change in the home price," and rates drifted 30bp higher *during* Lennar's quarter [26]. That is the equivalent of roughly a 3% price concession needed to hold pace. Freddie Mac's 30-year averaged **6.76%** on 10 Sep 2026, up from 6.71% a week earlier and **6.35% a year earlier** [19]. Industry-wide, 35% of builders cut prices in August and 63% used incentives [32]. MBA's Builder Application Survey had new-home purchase applications **−5.7% YoY in July** [33].

**The tell to watch on the call (Thursday 11am, not Wednesday night):** whether the incentive rate went *up* sequentially from 12.9%, and whether management repeats the "sustainable decline" language or retreats from it. Also: land take-down flexibility under the land-light structure, and Q4 starts/absorption guidance — the three things HousingWire says investors will focus on [26].

4. Fundamentals — what changed, what is at stake
text: **Segment mix.** Homebuilding dominates; Financial Services is the swing earner and is shrinking fast — $178m in Q3 FY25 against a $95–100m Q3 FY26 guide [13][11]. Multifamily contributed $18m in Q2 [11]. Financial Services is levered to mortgage volume and gain-on-sale; the buydown-heavy environment compresses it.

section: 4. Fundamentals — what changed, what is at stake
text: **Unit economics and operating discipline — the genuine bright spot.** Cycle time **121 days** in Q2, from 122 sequentially and 132 a year earlier, after hitting a company-record 126 days in Q3 FY25 [11][13]. Inventory **2.1 homes per community**, down from 3.0 sequentially; ~38,600 homes in inventory including ~3,500 completed unsold [11][34]. Starts ~20,600 in Q2 [34]. This is a company that has genuinely tightened its production loop; the problem is price, not pace.

section: 4. Fundamentals — what changed, what is at stake
text: **Margin trajectory.** 15.2% → 15.6% → guided ~16.0%. Sequentially improving, but 150bp below the year-ago quarter and roughly 900bp below the 2022 peak era. SG&A is going the wrong way YoY (8.2% → 8.8–9.0% guided) on digital-marketing and technology spend [14][11].

section: 4. Fundamentals — what changed, what is at stake
text: **Free cash flow and balance sheet — the uncomfortable pairing.** FCF for the quarter ending 31 May 2026 was **−$740.5m**, and FY2025 FCF was **$0.179bn, −92.2% vs 2024** [35]. Against that, Lennar repurchased **$736.8m of stock in H1 FY26** [36] — i.e. the buyback is not being funded out of current free cash flow. Cumulatively the multi-year programme has retired ~18.04% of shares for ~$5.97bn [35]. Debt-to-total-capital is a conservative 15.8% with $1.8bn homebuilding cash and $4.0bn homebuilding debt [11], and there is a 5.25% note due 2026 and a 5.0% due 2027 [36]. The balance sheet is not the risk; the cash-funded buyback into a declining-margin cycle is a legitimate capital-allocation

section: 4. Fundamentals — what changed, what is at stake
text: **What changed structurally.** Lennar completed the **Millrose Properties** spin-off in Feb 2025 — $5.6bn of land / 87,000 homesites and $1bn of cash off the balance sheet — converting Lennar to a land-light, just-in-time homesite model, with ~$900m of the cash contribution used by Millrose to take the Rausch Coleman land [37][38]. Q2 FY26 was described as the quarter that "tests the land-light model" [15]. The structure raises ROE in good times and, per the HousingWire framing, may *reduce* flexibility to slow production in bad ones because take-down schedules are contractual [26]. This is the least-understood part of the story and a plausible source of surprise in either direction.
